one_line: A short left-to-right ground-level transit where you trot along a solid floor, hopping three small spike beds, with a couple of floating platforms overhead that mostly serve to lift you to the coin and the raised east doorway.
structure: Horizontal corridor, west-to-east, 32x18 with an almost entirely empty upper two-thirds; both doors are mid-height gaps (rows 14-16) reached via short one-way platforms at row 15 on each side; the traversal itself happens on the bottom floor.
hazards: Three short spike beds (up-pointing, 3/3/2 tiles wide) sitting on the floor at roughly x=9-11, 17-19, 25-26; nothing else — no ceiling spikes, no shutters, no timing element. Each bed is a single jump or a dash to clear, with generous safe floor between them.
distinctive: The huge empty vertical space: 8 rows of nothing above the action, with two isolated one-way platforms (row 12 mid, row 9 right) that lead nowhere and give the room a half-drawn feel. The one genuine beat is the coin tucked two tiles above the eastern exit platform.
archetype_guess: spike-floor hop corridor (horizontal transit room)

one_line: You jog in along a bare basement corridor, then climb a narrow spiked chimney where the safe wall keeps flipping under you, top out over the divider, grab a coin tucked into the ceiling corner, and pick your way down an open right-hand hall past two spike beds to the east door.
structure: Split by a full-height wall at column 18, joined only by a low open corridor across the floor (rows 14-16) and over the top (row 1). Travel: west door (low left) -> east along the basement -> vertical wall-jump chimney (cols 13-17, rows 2-13) -> across the ceiling rightward -> descending open arena on the right -> east door (low right). Net shape: a tall U with a mandatory ascent in the middle.
hazards: No timed elements. Static spike walls line the chimney: right-facing spikes on its left wall at rows 8-9 and 12-13, left-facing spikes on its right wall at rows 10-11, so the clingable side alternates as you rise. Two up-facing spike beds on the right-hand floor (cols 21-22, 27-28) punish sloppy descents. One-way platforms (rows 4, 7, 10, 15) give bail-out ledges.
distinctive: The chimney's safe cling side alternates three times on the way up, so the wall-jump chain is a read-ahead puzzle rather than a rhythm — you must commit to the correct wall before each kick instead of ping-ponging freely.
archetype_guess: alternating-spike wall-jump chimney with open descent arena

one_line: You drop in through a hole in the ceiling into a mostly-empty vault, hop up a scattered staircase of one-way platforms to snag the coin tucked above a small spike bed, then climb back out the same hole — a short, low-pressure detour with a lot of dead air around it.
structure: Dead-end pocket entered from the ceiling: a 32x18 box split by two full-height pillars (col 10 and col 17). The player enters via the ceiling gap at cols 14-17, falls into the narrow middle chute, then travels right/up through a loose diagonal of one-way platforms in the wide right chamber; the whole left third (cols 1-9) is an empty unused shaft. Net travel is down-then-back-up, ending where it began.
hazards: Minimal: a single 3-tile up-spike bed on the floor at the bottom-right (row 17, cols 23-25), directly under the coin approach, so a missed landing off the small "--" ledge punishes you. No spike walls, no timing hazards, no shutters.
distinctive: It is a true ceiling-entry dead-end vault — the only way in is also the only way out, so the room is a there-and-back coin errand rather than a traversal — but the layout itself (scattered one-way platforms plus one spike bed) is generic.
archetype_guess: ceiling-drop dead-end coin vault with one-way-platform re-ascent

one_line: You duck under a hanging pillar, wall-jump a narrow chimney all the way to the open ceiling, dash across the top of a full-height partition to snag a coin on a high ledge, then commit to a long drop into a spike-floored chamber, aiming for the one safe corner beside the gated east door.
structure: Left-to-right traversal built around a vertical detour: a low west corridor, a 4-tile-wide chimney shaft (between the hanging pillar at col 9 and the floor-to-y60 partition at col 14) that you climb ~7 tiles to the open upper third of the room, an overhead crossing eastward across ledge stubs, and then a tall open east chamber you must descend to the far-right corner. Effectively a U/n-shaped route: east low, up, east high, down.
hazards: A single spike bed: 14 tiles of upward spikes filling the entire floor of the east chamber (cols 15-28), leaving only a 2-tile solid ledge at the far right by the exit door. No spike walls, no timed elements. All danger is in the descent-and-landing, not the climb.
distinctive: The room is a lock in disguise: it demands *both* wall-jump and dash (a wall-only loadout is provably unable to cross), and its east door is coin-gated at 55, so the geometry, the ability check and the progression gate all coincide in one room. Mechanically the standout beat is that the reward for the climb is a one-way commitment — once you cross the partition roof the only way out is a drop over a full spike floor onto a two-tile ledge.
archetype_guess: chimney-ascent gate room (wall-jump shaft + overhead dash crossing + spike-floor descent)

one_line: You jog across an empty entry hall, then climb a narrow four-tile chimney whose two walls are studded with anti-phased spikes so you must wall-jump on alternating safe bands, pop out on a top ledge, dash one clean gap right to the coin, and drop back down through a stack of one-way platforms over a long spike bed to the east door.
structure: Three-part left-to-right room: a wide empty west approach chamber (cols 1-11, west door at floor level), a tall 4-tile-wide vertical chimney in the middle (cols 14-17, climbed bottom-to-top), then a right-hand descent chamber (cols 20-30) where you work back down through stacked one-way platforms to the east door at floor level. Net travel: east, up, then east and back down.
hazards: Spike-lined chimney: the left face (col 13) is spiked at rows 2-4, 8-10 and 14 with safe stone only at rows 6-7 and 12-13; the right face (col 18) is spiked at rows 6-7 and 11-13 with safe stone at rows 4-5 and 8-10. The two faces are deliberately anti-phased, so a continuous same-wall climb is fatal and you must swap sides at each band. In the right chamber a ten-tile upward spike bed (row 8, cols 18-27) sits under the descent line, with a single up-spike at the right end of the lower platform (row 11, col 30) punishing a sloppy landing. No timed/shutter hazards.
distinctive: The anti-phased spike chimney: the safe stone on the two facing walls never overlaps vertically, so the climb reads as a forced left-right-left rhythm rather than a free wall-jump shaft — and the coin is gated behind exactly one horizontal dash off the top ledge, giving the room a clear two-beat identity (rhythm climb, then one committed dash).
archetype_guess: alternating spike-wall chimney ascent with a dash-gated top pickup and platform descent

one_line: You drop through the ceiling into a narrow stone chimney, fall twelve tiles to snatch coin 18 off the floor, then wall-jump the whole way back up the same shaft to leave the way you came — with two thirds of the room being empty hall you never touch.
structure: Dead-end cul-de-sac hanging off bell-switchback: a single ceiling door (cols 14-17) feeds a 5-tile-wide, 15-tile-deep vertical shaft walled by col 11 and col 17, sealed at row 17. Travel is down-then-back-up through the same throat. To the right of col 17 sits a large 13x16 empty hall with one stray one-way platform at row 9, and to the left of col 11 another 10-wide empty column; neither is on any route.
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes, no shutters, no moving parts. The only failure mode is a botched wall-jump chain that drops you back to the shaft floor for a retry, which costs nothing.
distinctive: The shaft-bottom coin placement forces the ascent to be the real content: the exit is the door you entered by, so the room is a pure "climb back out of the hole you jumped into" test that hard-gates on the wall glove. The one-way platform at row 5 is a mid-shaft breather that quietly makes that climb safe.
archetype_guess: dead-end coin cache in a wall-jump chimney (drop-and-reclimb niche)

one_line: You jog in along a wide open mid-height band, thread a narrow spike-flanked one-way gap in the floor down to the Bell Niche, then jog back out east — the tall half of the room above you never gets touched.
structure: Wide east-west corridor band across the lower-middle (row 14) of a 32x18 room, with a vertical branch down through the floor at cols 14-17; the upper two-thirds is tall dead space split by two full-height pillars (cols 10 and 13) forming a 2-tile chimney, plus a solid ledge and one-way shelf in the upper right. Travel is west-to-east, with a there-and-back detour downward.
hazards: Two lone up-facing spikes (row 16, cols 13 and 18) bracket the floor exit; the one-way platform strip between them is the only safe drop lane. No spike walls, no timed elements. Density is very low and purely a framing device for the floor door.
distinctive: The floor exit is a spike-bracketed slot you must line up on before committing to the drop. Otherwise almost everything in the room — the whole chimney and the upper-right platforms — is scenery you never interact with, and the room holds no coins of its own.
archetype_guess: three-way junction / fork hub with a gated floor drop

one_line: A wide, airy hall where you enter mid-height from the west, hop a scattered zig-zag of one-way platforms up to a coin tucked under the top-right ledge, then fall back down to the east door — with a patch of ceiling spikes that quietly forbids the obvious straight-up jump.
structure: Mostly empty 32x18 arena; nominal travel is west-to-east through mid-height doors (side-wall gaps at rows 14-16), with an optional vertical detour: five short one-way platforms staircasing left-right-left-right up to the top-right ledge, then a long free-fall back to the east exit platform.
hazards: Two upward spike beds on the floor (cols 9-12 and 17-20) punishing missed drops in the lower middle, plus a 4-tile downward spike strip on the ceiling directly above the mid-right platform, which blocks the direct vertical continuation of the climb and forces a leftward hop to the row-7 platform before swinging right to the coin ledge.
distinctive: The ceiling spikes sit exactly above the platform you'd instinctively jump straight up from, turning a plain staircase into a small S-shaped reroute; coin 35 at the top right is only reachable through that detour.
archetype_guess: open-arena one-way-platform climb with a coin detour (gallery/hall family)

one_line: You drop in from Crossroads below, then grind up a narrow three-tile spiked chute in a wall-jump chain, threading a band where spikes jut from both walls at once, to pop out at the top and claim the winged boots (dash) plus a coin before dropping into the right-hand chamber and leaving east.
structure: Three vertical bays sharing a full-width bottom corridor (row 17): a large sealed empty box on the left (cols 1-12, unreachable dead volume), a tall 3-wide ascent chute in the centre (cols 15-17, rows 2-16), and an open right chamber (cols 19-30) with a ceiling shelf at row 5. Direction of travel is up the centre chute, then right and down; entry is the floor gap at cols 14-17 (from Crossroads), exit is the east opening at rows 14-16 (to Underpass).
hazards: Spike walls only, no floor beds and no timers: right-pointing spikes stud the left wall of the chute at rows 2-5, 9-10 and 15-16, left-pointing spikes face them at rows 9-10, plus a downward spike in the ceiling at col 14. The rows 9-10 double-sided pinch is the crux — both walls are lethal simultaneously, so you must clear that band in one airborne beat rather than continuing the wall-jump chain through it.
distinctive: The dash ability is locked behind a wall-jump-only spiked chimney: you earn the movement upgrade with the movement tool you already have, and the room is authored to be unenterable/unrewarding until the boots are taken (room gating on winged_boots).
archetype_guess: spiked wall-jump chimney ability vault (ascent chute + reward alcove)

one_line: A west-to-east ground transit interrupted by a single tall pillar you must ladder over on staggered one-way platforms, with an optional platform climb up the right side to a coin tucked near the ceiling.
structure: Wide open hall, primary travel west→east along the floor, bisected by a 7-tile-tall solid pillar at column 18 that forces a short up-and-over; a secondary vertical ladder of platforms rises on the east half to a ceiling-level coin. Effectively an L: cross low, then climb.
hazards: Almost none. One 3-tile up-spike patch on the floor immediately east of the pillar (cols 19-21), which only bites if you drop straight down off the pillar instead of carrying momentum east. Everything else is empty air with a solid floor to catch failed jumps.
distinctive: The pillar-plus-spike-shadow pinch: the only moment with a real fail state is the landing choice coming off the pillar top, where the safe pad is a couple of tiles further east than the lazy drop.
archetype_guess: open-air platform ladder with an optional ceiling coin (dash-ladder / coin tower family)

one_line: You walk in low from the west, run into a tall unbroken wall, and grind your way up a wide two-walled chimney to the ceiling before hopping down a staircase of one-way platforms to the east exit.
structure: Left-to-right transit with a big vertical detour: a low west corridor (rows 14-16) dead-ends against a full-height wall at col 17; between the col-10 and col-17 walls sits a 6-tile-wide open chimney you climb ~11 tiles to the open ceiling band (rows 1-2), cross east above the wall, then descend the right-hand chamber on six staggered one-way platforms to the east door at rows 14-16. Cols 1-9 are a large empty dead-space chamber with nothing in it.
hazards: None at all — no spikes, no shutters. The only failure is losing a wall-jump chain and falling back to the floor for a free retry.
distinctive: The 6-tile-wide chimney with two facing climbable walls — too wide to alternate comfortably, so it reads as a sustained single-wall ascent and is the room's one real ask; the coin (dungeon-coin-17, at 204,30) is parked high on the right, rewarding you for actually reaching the top rather than shortcutting.
archetype_guess: wall-jump ascent + platform-staircase descent transit room

one_line: A wide, almost entirely empty hall you sprint straight through west-to-east, with one small step-up-and-hop over a short spike bed and a coin dangling above a floating platform as the only reason to slow down.
structure: Horizontal ground-level corridor/hall, 32x18, travelled west to east (doors are full 3-tile gaps in both side walls at floor level). The bottom wall is a single unbroken floor; the entire upper two-thirds is open air with five short one-way platforms scattered in a loose rising right-ward staircase (cols 5-8 and 14-21 low, 10-13, 15-18, 20-23 higher) that no route requires.
hazards: A single up-facing spike bed, 5 tiles wide, sitting on a 1-tile-high block near mid-room (cols 14-18). Nothing else. It is clearable with an ordinary running jump, and the platform two tiles above it offers a second free line over the top, so the hazard is nearly optional.
distinctive: The vertical emptiness: three-quarters of the room is unused air with decorative platforms leading nowhere, while the actual route is a flat floor run. The one coin (col ~20, above the long low platform) is the only thing that uses that space.
archetype_guess: flat-floor connector corridor with a token spike hop

one_line: A wide open hall you cross at floor level, but the coin bait pulls you into a rising staircase of tiny one-way platforms under a spiked ceiling, where each gap is too far to jump and must be dashed.
structure: Wide 32x18 arena traversed west-to-east at the bottom (both doors are 2-tile gaps at rows 13-14), with an optional diagonal ascending relay of three short one-way platforms climbing left-to-right (cols 12-15 @ row 11, cols 20-23 @ row 8, cols 27-29 @ row 5) toward a coin in the top-right corner.
hazards: Floor spike beds in three separated patches (cols 8-11, 16-19, 24-26) with a small 3-tile solid pillar between the first two; a band of downward spikes across the upper middle (cols 17-25, row 3) caps the arc over the second relay hop. No timed elements.
distinctive: The coin sits tucked between the down-spike ceiling band and the topmost platform, so the last hop must be a flat dash rather than a jump — you can't arc into it.
archetype_guess: open arena with optional ascending dash-relay to a corner collectible

one_line: A calm, hazard-free open hall where you hop up a staircase of one-way platforms past a lone stone pillar to claim the climbing gloves tucked in the high-right alcove, then drop back down and stroll out east.
movement_verbs: wall-jump (first taste, on the central pillar)
structure: Wide 32x18 open cavern, west-to-east traversal with a rightward-and-upward staircase: a low platform at (3-8, r15), a mid platform at (11-15, r13), a 4-tile solid pillar at x=17 (r11-14), a platform at (18-22, r10), and the reward ledge at (24-28, r7); a ground-level ledge at (24-29, r15) catches the descent. Doors are floor-level gaps in both side walls (rows 14-15).
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes, no shutters, no pits. Failure means falling to the empty floor and re-climbing, with zero damage.
distinctive: It is the glove vault: the climbing-gloves pickup sits at (254,44) on the top-right ledge, and the room is deliberately toothless so acquiring the ability is the whole event. The lone free-standing pillar at x=17 is the only vertical face in the room and reads as a "try the new toy here" surface.
archetype_guess: ability-pickup vault / ascending one-way-platform staircase

one_line: A wide, airy dead-end larder: you drop in through the ceiling, zigzag down a staircase of one-way platforms into a pocket under a right-hand overhang to grab a coin, then hop the same platforms straight back out.
structure: Single 32x18 open box entered through a ceiling gap (cols 14-17) with no other exit — a there-and-back vertical detour. Interior is a loose alternating-left/right staircase of five 4-5 tile one-way platforms (rows 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) spaced 2 tiles apart, opening into a large empty lower chamber; a solid overhang at row 15 covers the right third, with one more platform at row 16 leading into the pocket beneath it where the coin sits (tile ~29,16).
hazards: Almost none: a single 2-tile up-spike bed on the floor at row 17, cols 14-15, directly under the entry column — a token punishment for falling straight down without steering, and easily avoided.
distinctive: The room is essentially all air: the coin's pocket under the row-15 overhang is the only piece of real geometry, and it isn't defended by anything.
archetype_guess: optional coin cul-de-sac / drop-shaft with one-way platform staircase

one_line: You drop in through a ceiling chute into a big, mostly empty box, float down a scatter of one-way platforms to scoop coin 8, wander up the open left side for coin 9, then climb back out the way you came — nothing can hurt you and nothing can go wrong.
structure: Dead-end 32x18 open hall entered from a narrow ceiling chute (cols 14-16, walled by col 13 and col 17 for the top 3 rows) that opens out into a single undivided room; travel is down-then-back-up, with a loose right-to-left descending staircase of one-way platforms (rows 7, 9, 11, 13, 15) and a lone 7-tile solid block at row 5 left. Same ceiling door in and out — it is a pocket off Crossroads, not a through-route.
hazards: None. Zero spikes, no pits, no shutters; the floor is plain solid and every fall is survivable, so no failure state exists.
distinctive: The entry chute with its one-way platform lid — the only committed geometry — is over in three seconds, after which the room is a large empty vault holding two unguarded coins (8 mid-air above the row-13 platform, 9 tucked beside the row-5 solid block).
archetype_guess: unguarded coin-cache pocket / open one-way-platform vault

one_line: A flat west-to-east sprint over a 22-tile bed of upward spikes, where the only respite is a handful of scattered one-way platforms floating well overhead, so it plays as one long committed dash-and-jump gauntlet with almost nowhere safe to stop.
structure: Wide flat corridor, horizontal left-to-right travel; west and east doors both sit at the floor band (rows 14-17), with a mostly empty tall airspace above and sparse floating one-way platforms as the only footholds.
hazards: A near-continuous upward spike bed across the floor (cols 6-27 of the bottom traversable row), plus a short downward-spike ceiling cluster (cols 21-27, high up) that punishes over-jumping on the right side. No timed elements.
distinctive: The spike floor spans virtually the entire room while the safe platforms are 4-5 tiles above it and unevenly spaced (cols 11-12, 17-18, 24-25, 28-30), so the crossing is airborne and dash-dependent rather than a rhythmic hop chain — and the short one-way strip at the far west (cols 1-5) is the only real staging ground.
archetype_guess: spike-floor horizontal run / dash gauntlet

structure: Left-to-right (west door row 14 → east door row 14) horizontal traverse across a spike-bed floor, interrupted by a full-height pillar at column 17 that forces a vertical detour: a ~30px-wide wall-jump chimney between the col-13 wall and the pillar (rows 7-13), then a run along the top of a 5-tile ceiling shelf (row 8, cols 17-21), then a drop back down to the platform hops on the east side. Coin 55 hangs in a tall right-hand shaft (cols 25-30) just above the last platform.
hazards: A near-continuous bed of upward spikes forms the floor (row 17, cols 7-16 and 18-28), leaving only a safe one-way platform strip on the far left (cols 1-6) and a solid ledge at cols 29-30. No spike walls, no timed elements — all danger is "don't touch the ground".
one_line: A spike-floor crossing that suddenly turns vertical: you hop one-way platforms east until a floor-to-ceiling pillar stops you, wall-jump chain up a narrow chimney to run along an overhead shelf, then drop back onto the platform chain and pop up a side shaft for the coin.
distinctive: The col-17 pillar welded to the row-8 ceiling shelf: it makes a horizontal room briefly become a climbing room, and the 30px chimney beside it is the only way through, so the wall-jump is mandatory rather than optional.
archetype_guess: spike-floor platform-hop corridor with a mandatory mid-room wall-jump chimney

one_line: A short dead-end side-pocket: you pop up through a one-way platform in the floor and zigzag left-right up three staggered ledges between two spike-faced pillars to grab coin 32 in the top-right corner, then drop back out the way you came.
structure: Roughly 32x18 chamber entered and exited through the same floor gap (cols ~14-17) — a bottom-up zigzag switchback climb, then a reversal back down. Two full-height pillars (col 10 rows 9-17, col 17 rows 4-14) split the space into a left alley, a central duct, and a right bay; three one-way ledges alternate sides (row 13 right, row 9 centre-left, row 5 right) so travel is up-and-alternating rather than a straight shaft. Dead end: only connection is floor to Foundry Fork's ceiling.
hazards: Spike walls only, no floors or ceilings of spikes: right-pointing spikes on the left pillar's upper face (col 10, rows 5-8) and left-pointing spikes on the right pillar's inner face (col 17, rows 11-12). Both are on the inner walls of the duct, so they punish wall-grabbing or overshooting a hop but are entirely avoidable if you land cleanly on the one-ways. No timed elements. Effectively a zero-death room for a competent player — retry friction rather than threat, matching the assessment doc's "light hazard / passable" note.
distinctive: Facing spike walls make the central duct a "climb without touching the walls" corridor — an inversion of wall-jump instinct — but the gaps are generous enough that the idea never bites.
archetype_guess: dead-end one-way-platform switchback coin closet with decorative wall spikes

one_line: A calm, hazard-free four-way hub where you land in an open central chamber, pick a direction — walk out east or west, drop through the one-way floor hatch, or wall-jump up the narrow central chimney to the ceiling door — and grab a single coin on the way.
structure: Symmetric hub arena: a 4-tile-wide vertical chimney (cols 14-17) walled by pillars runs from the ceiling door down into an open lower chamber; left/right doors sit at mid-height (rows 14-16) with short one-way ledges leading to each, a central one-way platform bridges the middle, and the floor door is a one-way hatch directly below the chimney. Travel is omnidirectional.
hazards: None — zero spikes, no timed elements, no fall danger.
distinctive: It is a genuine 4-way junction (west/east/ceiling/floor) with mirror symmetry, and the ceiling route is a wall-jump chimney that gates progress on the glove; also advertises the 21-coin gate.
archetype_guess: symmetric four-way hub / junction breather room

one_line: A west-to-east traverse that is really one big up-and-over: you run into a dead-end shaft, wall-jump your way ~13 tiles up a full-height divider, then pick your way back down the east side via two one-way platforms without dropping onto the spike bed at the bottom.
structure: Horizontal corridor (west door <-> east door, both at the low rows) interrupted by a vertical chimney: a full-height solid column at x=16 spanning rows 4-17 splits the room, with a shorter column at x=10 forming a ~5-tile-wide shaft on its west side. Travel is west -> up the shaft -> over the top (open rows 1-3) -> staged descent on the east half -> east door.
hazards: A single spike bed on the floor of the east half (row 17, x=19-22, up-facing), positioned directly under the natural fall line from the top of the divider. No spike walls, no timed elements. It punishes a careless plummet rather than the climb itself.
distinctive: The east descent is a designed staircase of one-way platforms (a long ledge at row 6, a shorter one at row 15 further east) that exists purely to steer you around the spikes below - the drop is a routing puzzle, not a freefall.
archetype_guess: up-and-over divider wall / chimney climb with staged platform descent

one_line: A big S-shaped victory lap: you wall-jump twelve tiles up a tight left shaft, run the ceiling gutter, drop down a blind chute, squeeze through a one-tile slot, then chimney back up over a full-width spike floor to the crown perched on a top-right shelf.
structure: Terminal single-door chamber, ~32x18, split by a full-height divider at col 18 into a left ascent shaft and a right chimney. Travel is a circuit: enter bottom-left (west door, rows 14-16), climb north up the col-1..6 shaft past the col-7 pillar, run east along the open ceiling band (rows 2-4) over the col-12 wall, drop south down the cols 13-17 chute to row 13, thread the single-tile slot under the col-18 divider, then ascend the right chamber's cols 19-27 chimney (col-23 pillar, col-28 wall) back to row 2 and hop east onto the crown shelf at cols 29-30.
hazards: One hazard, used as the room's whole threat model: an unbroken spike bed along row 17 from col 13 to col 30 — the floor of the entire right half. Every mistake in the descent chute, the slot, or the final chimney drops you onto it. No timed shutters, no spike walls, and the left half is completely hazard-free.
distinctive: It is the game's terminal room: no coins at all, one west door and no exit, and the only pickup is the crown (Rect 285,14) sitting on a small top-right shelf — so the whole space reads as a vertical lap of honour whose only failure state is the spike floor beneath it. The gating is authored (64 coins + both traversal abilities on the Gatehouse door), not geometric, so the geometry itself is a pure climbing gauntlet.
archetype_guess: divided twin-shaft ascent / finale climbing gauntlet over a spike floor

one_line: You slip under a divider wall into a narrow 3-tile chimney whose two walls are spiked in alternating vertical bands, forcing a strict zig-zag wall-jump chain up ~14 tiles, then spill out into open air at the top and drop down the right-hand chamber onto one-way platforms to the east door.
structure: Three-zone left-to-right traverse with a vertical spine: a tall but empty left chamber (cols 1-9) at entry, a narrow enclosed chimney (cols 12-14) climbed bottom-to-top, and a large open right chamber descended to the east door. Net travel is east, but the path is up-then-down.
hazards: Spike walls only, no floor spikes and no timed elements. Right-facing spikes on the chimney's left wall at rows 5-7 and 11-13; left-facing spikes on its right wall at rows 8-10 and 14-16. The safe wall therefore alternates in three-tile bands, so the ascent punishes clinging to the same side twice.
distinctive: The staggered alternating spike bands inside the chimney: the geometry enforces a genuine left-right-left wall-jump rhythm rather than letting you hug one wall, and the safe side flips exactly at the cadence a natural chain wants — satisfying when read correctly, instantly fatal when mistimed.
archetype_guess: spike-lined wall-jump chimney (vertical glove-gated climb embedded in a horizontal traverse)

one_line: A wide-open hall you cross left-to-right by hopping three spike beds on the floor, with an optional diagonal staircase of five sparse one-way platforms climbing to a coin tucked under a row of ceiling spikes in the top right.
structure: Single-screen west-to-east corridor/arena: full-width open air, floor at the bottom, doors as tall gaps in both side walls at the bottom four rows. Layered above the floor is an ascending diagonal chain of one-way platforms (cols 3-6 @ y140, 11-13 @ y110, 18-20 @ y80, 25-27 @ y50, plus a stub at 28-29 @ y140), so the room reads as ground-level slalom + optional upward climb to the top-right corner.
hazards: Three spike beds (up-facing, 4 tiles each) along the floor at cols 7-10, 14-17, 21-24, with safe gaps exactly beneath each platform; plus an 8-tile down-facing spike ceiling strip (cols 16-23) hanging in mid-air over the middle of the climb, which caps the airspace on the way to the coin.
distinctive: The spike gaps in the floor sit directly under the platforms, so the ground route and the coin climb share the same rhythm of landing spots — and the floating down-spike bar forces the ascent to stay low and diagonal rather than jumping straight up.
archetype_guess: spike-floor hop corridor with an optional platform-staircase coin climb

one_line: You drop in through the only door in the ceiling, steer past a bank of side-facing spikes on the way down, and then have to earn the whole descent back with wall-jumps and one-way platforms because the way in is also the only way out.
structure: Dead-end vault, 32x18, entered from the ceiling (gap at cols 14-17). Two full-height interior walls (col 10 rows 5-17, col 17 rows 3-13) split it into three vertical bands: a narrow middle shaft (cols 11-16) directly under the door, a wide right chamber (cols 18-30) laddered by one-way platforms at row 5 and row 13, and a tall sealed left pit (cols 1-9) reachable only by going over the col-10 wall at rows 2-4. Travel is down then back up the same room.
hazards: Sparse: three left-facing spikes on the col-16 wall face at rows 8-10, positioned to punish hugging the right side of the middle shaft during the fall and the climb-out. No spike beds, no timed elements; the real hazard is geometry (the 12-tile left pit and the 8-tile gap between the row-13 and row-5 platforms).
distinctive: It is a true one-door cache: the ceiling gap is entrance and exit, so the room is a there-and-back where the climb out is the actual challenge, and the col-17 wall exists mainly as a wall-jump ladder between the two one-way shelves.
archetype_guess: one-door dead-end coin vault / drop-in-and-climb-out chamber

one_line: You walk in from the west, cross a short ledge, and either drop through a one-way slot in the floor to the Cullet Cache or hop a two-tile spike pair and keep walking east — the whole upper two-thirds of the room, with its platforms and ceiling spikes, is scenery you never touch.
structure: Wide horizontal junction box, 32x18, but only the bottom three rows are live: west door (rows 14-16) → floor ledge → east door (rows 14-16), with a third exit straight down through a 4-tile gap in the bottom wall. Travel is left-to-right with an optional downward branch.
hazards: Essentially none in play: one 2-tile up-spike pair (^^) mid-floor that a normal jump clears, plus a 5-tile ceiling spike cluster (vvvvv) at row 6 that sits in dead airspace. The drop slot's lips are unspiked, so committing to the descent costs nothing.
distinctive: The three-way branch itself (west/east/floor to a coin cache) — but it is presented as a free choice with no cost on any arm, so mechanically nothing distinguishes it.
archetype_guess: flat-floor three-way junction with drop-through slot and decorative upper story

one_line: A wide, mostly empty hall you walk straight across from the west door to the east door in a couple of seconds, unless you choose to sidestep into the narrow central floor slot and drop to the Coin Duct below.
structure: A 32x18 open arena crossed horizontally: a full-width open band at rows 14-16 links the west and east side doors, with a 4-tile floor gap (cols 14-17) in the bottom wall as a third, downward exit. Everything above row 13 is empty air with two orphan one-way platforms (row 8 right side, row 12 centre) that the main route never needs.
hazards: Two single up-facing spikes embedded in the floor lips immediately flanking the drop slot (row 17, cols 12 and 19). They only matter if you approach the hole badly or try to climb back out onto the ledge; the horizontal route never touches them. No spike beds, walls, or shutters.
distinctive: The three-way branch (west / east / straight down) with the spiked lips making the descent the one committed choice — but the branch is the entire content, and there is no coin or pickup anywhere to reward exploring it.
archetype_guess: three-way junction / traversal hub with a spiked floor-drop slot

one_line: A wide, mostly empty hall whose floor is a spike bed: you sprint off the west ledge, dash a 60px gap onto a three-tile island in the middle, then repeat the same dash to the east ledge, with a spike bank overhead keeping the arc flat.
structure: Wide flat west-to-east corridor along the bottom of a 32x18 box; safe ground on the solid bottom row at x0-8 and x24-31, a 15-tile spike bed between them broken only by a 3-tile one-way platform island at x15-17. West and east doors both sit at floor level (rows 13-16). The upper two thirds of the room is completely empty, unused space.
hazards: Up-spikes fill the floor either side of the mid island (x9-14 and x18-23); a matching bank of down-spikes hangs at row 6 over the same span, capping the arc height. No shutters, no moving parts.
distinctive: It is a pure dash gate rather than a puzzle — two identical 60px spike gaps that a jump alone cannot clear, existing to prove you have the dash. demo_dungeon.rs even carries a test asserting no wall-jump-only route exists under the same search budget. No coins, no pickups; only west (Climbers' Gallery) and east (Gale Landing) doors.
archetype_guess: flat spike-bed dash-gap crossing (dash-gate corridor)

one_line: A short west-to-east ground run that ends at a narrow, fully spike-lined pit you must dash across to reach the gated east door — one committed leap under a big, mostly empty ceiling.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor along the bottom (rows 14-17) travelling west to east, with a large empty two-chamber hall above it split by a vertical wall at col 21 and a couple of one-way platforms on the right; the only real play is the floor-level ledge-gap-ledge sequence.
hazards: One three-tile gap between the two floor ledges, lined on every surface: right-facing spikes on the left wall of the pit, left-facing spikes on the right wall, up-spikes on its floor. A row of down-spikes hangs in the left upper chamber but sits far above the travel line and is easy to ignore. No timed hazards.
distinctive: The pit is a mouth of spikes — walls and floor all hostile — so there is no "clip the edge and recover" outcome; combined with the east door needing 24 coins and the dash itself, it reads as a deliberate skill-check seal for the dash region.
archetype_guess: gate/seal room: single spike-pit dash gap guarding a region door

one_line: You walk in from the west onto a completely flat, hazard-free floor, jog straight to the east door in a couple of seconds, and the only other thing to do is wall-jump up a short 4-tile chimney into a huge empty box of dead air where the ceiling door hangs unreachably far above you.
structure: Wide rectangular box, 32x18. Travel is primarily horizontal west→east along an open 3-tile-tall floor strip (rows 14-16) that spans the whole width unobstructed. Two short vertical pillars (col 11 and col 16, rows 8-14) hang down from mid-height, forming a 4-tile-wide (40px) chimney between them plus a small ledge (row 8, cols 16-19); above row 8 the entire upper two-thirds of the room is one empty 30x7 hall with the ceiling door gap at cols 14-17.
hazards: None whatsoever — not a single spike tile, no shutters, nothing that can kill you.
distinctive: The vertical "fork" branch is broken/vestigial: the chimney tops out at row 8 and the ceiling door is ~70px above open, featureless air with jump rise ~40px and no walls to chain off, so the advertised third exit reads as unreachable from the grid.
archetype_guess: flat horizontal transit hall with a token wall-jump chimney (three-door junction room)
dead-end coin vault: descend-and-return shaft hugging a spike wall
distinctive: A full-height (rows 6-17) right-facing spike wall on column 24 that forms one side of the narrow platform-ladder shaft holding the coin — every drop and every climb-out is taken with spikes at your shoulder.
hazards: A single continuous vertical spike wall (12 tiles of '>' on col 24) facing east into the right-hand shaft; no spike beds, ceilings or shutters. All danger is lateral proximity while dropping through and re-climbing the one-way platform ladder.
one_line: You fall in through the ceiling into a big empty hall, sprint right, then thread down a narrow platform ladder pinned against a tall spike wall to grab the coin at the bottom — and have to climb the same spiked shaft back out, since this room is a dead end.
structure: Two-part room: a wide, near-empty 22-tile-wide left hall (only a few short floating '#' ledges at rows 8, 11, 14, 17 that nothing forces you to use) and a narrow 6-tile-wide right shaft running the full height, rungs of one-way platforms alternating left/right. Travel is down-then-right-then-down, and back up the same way. Single opening: a ceiling gap at cols 14-17 leading to Split Furnace; no floor or side doors.

one_line: A wide, empty hall where you drift in from one open side, hop up a lazy zigzag of three floating one-way platforms, and pop out the ceiling — never once threatened by anything.
movement_verbs: short dash to cover horizontal offset
structure: Wide 32x18 arena/junction: an open low corridor band (rows 14-16) crossing west-east with a one-way platform at each end, two low floor bumps, and above it an open sky with three staggered one-way ledges (row 12 centre-left, row 9 right, row 6 centre) forming a zigzag ascent to a ceiling door at cols 14-17. Travel is both lateral (W<->E) and upward.
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes of any kind, no shutters, no pits (the floor is fully solid). Zero fail states short of missing a ledge and falling back to the floor.
distinctive: It is a three-way junction (west, east, ceiling) whose upward branch is a free-form zigzag over a huge empty vault — the emptiness is the identity, and it reads as breathing room rather than a challenge.
archetype_guess: hazardless three-way junction hub with staggered one-way platform ascent

one_line: A left-to-right traverse that stalls at a narrow spiked chimney: you wall-jump up a five-tile-wide flue past spikes that alternate left and right wall, then pop into a tall vault to snag the gate coin before dropping out the east side.
structure: Three vertical compartments separated by full-height walls, joined only along the open bottom two rows: a wide dead-ish left hall (cols 1-9) with a one-way ledge, a tall narrow wall-jump flue (cols 11-15) rising the whole room height, and a vault chamber (cols 17-24) holding the coin, then a plain right shaft to the east door. Travel is west-to-east at floor level with one mandatory-feeling vertical excursion up the flue and back down.
hazards: Sparse and mostly decorative: two right-facing spikes on the flue's left wall (rows 6, 10) and two left-facing spikes on its right wall (rows 8, 12), forcing a staggered rather than metronomic wall-jump chain; a short up-spike bed (cols 12-14) in the floor pit below the flue; a row of down-spikes under the vault's ceiling that you pass beside, not through. Nothing sits on the actual through-route, so a fumble usually costs a re-climb rather than a life.
distinctive: The alternating left/right wall spikes in the flue: they break the rhythm of the wall-jump chain so you must swap sides on a specific beat instead of hammering the same two walls. That, plus coin 39 being the gate key for the east door, is the room's whole identity.
archetype_guess: spiked wall-jump chimney with side-vault coin detour

one_line: A wide, mostly empty hall you cross at floor level between two side doors, or — if you want the ceiling exit — zig-zag up six scattered one-way platforms over two spike beds, with each hop offset far enough sideways that a missed landing drops you all the way back to the spikes.
structure: 32x18 open arena with a solid floor, functioning as a three-way junction: west and east doors at row 14 (a flat, near-instant left-right traverse) plus a ceiling door at cols 14-17. The optional/route-target ascent is a right-then-left slalom up a staircase of one-way platforms (cols 4-8 @r15 → 12-17 @r12 → 21-26 @r9 → 14-18 @r7 → 14-18 @r4 → ceiling gap), with a second r15 platform at cols 26-29 giving an alternate start from the east door.
hazards: Two short spike beds on the floor (row 17, cols 9-12 and 19-22), upward-pointing only. They sit directly under the middle of the climb, so they punish falls rather than gating any path — the horizontal traverse walks past them untouched.
distinctive: The lateral offsets: the r12→r9 and r9→r7 hops swing you ~9 tiles right then ~7 back left, so the climb reads as a genuine zig-zag rather than a straight ladder, and the top two platforms stack directly under the ceiling gap for a clean finishing double-hop.
archetype_guess: one-way-platform ascent junction over a spike floor

one_line: A quick left-to-right hop across two one-way ledges and a single stepping-stone platform floating over a spike bed, all crammed into the bottom four rows of a room whose upper two-thirds is a vast, completely empty void.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor, west-to-east, played entirely in the bottom band (rows 14-17): left one-way platform (cols 3-9), a raised stepping-stone platform (row 12, cols 13-17) offset upward, then a right one-way platform (cols 23-29). Doors are full-height gaps in the west and east walls at rows 14-16. Rows 1-11 are entirely empty air with no content.
hazards: A single upward spike bed on the floor (row 17, cols 10-22) sitting directly under the central gap — the only hazard, and the only thing making the two dashes matter.
distinctive: The dramatic wasted space: ~two-thirds of the 32x18 grid is dead empty air, and the actual room is a thin ribbon along the bottom. The one real idea is the up-then-down rhythm of the offset middle platform.
archetype_guess: spike-pit gap-crossing corridor (one-way ledges + stepping stone)

one_line: A deliberate breather: you walk in from the west, hop up two broad stone steps onto the crest of a ziggurat beneath a hollow stone gate-block, then step down the far side to the 64-coin crown door — no hazards, no failure, just a processional approach to the finale.
structure: Symmetric west-to-east crossing over a three-tier stepped ziggurat/mound (rows 16-17 widest, 14-15 narrower, 12-13 crest), with doors as bottom-left and bottom-right wall gaps at the same height; a hollow 6x7 stone blockhouse floats above the crest like a gate arch, and a ladder of one-way platforms occupies the empty upper-left third entirely off-route.
hazards: None whatsoever — zero spikes, zero pits, zero timing. The only "gate" is the authored 64-coin requirement on the east door (DEMO_DUNGEON_CROWN_GATE_REQUIREMENT), plus an ALL_CURRENT traversal-methods flag that the geometry itself never enforces.
distinctive: The ziggurat-plus-floating-gatehouse silhouette: architecture doing the storytelling instead of mechanics, and a room whose test suite explicitly asserts the route cannot die and needs neither wall-jump nor dash.
archetype_guess: Ceremonial hazard-free gate antechamber / stepped processional approach

one_line: You come in low on the west floor, jog east and hop a token spike pair onto a small ledge, then do the room's real work — an eleven-tile wall-jump climb up the face of a tall pillar inside a five-wide chimney — mantle over the top for a free coin, and then just fall down the wide-open east half, ticking two platforms on the way to the exit.
structure: Left-to-right traversal with an up-and-over profile: low western floor run (cols 1-11, entirely empty), a 1-tile ledge step at col 12, a 5-tile-wide vertical chimney between the col-12 pillar (rows 3-13) and the col-18 pillar (rows 5-16) climbed to the ceiling, then a large open east chamber fallen down through to the east door. Both doors are 3-tile-tall openings at rows 14-16, so entry and exit are at the same low height while the path arcs to the top of the room.
hazards: Minimal: a single pair of upward spikes (row 16, cols 14-15) sitting on the raised ledge in front of the climbing wall. One easy hop clears them. No spike walls, no shutters, and the entire east half and the whole climb are hazard-free — the danger is falling, not dying.
distinctive: The tall enclosed chimney between two offset pillars: a ~110px climb that far exceeds a 40px jump and must be chained on the pillar face, with a mid-height rest platform (row 7) and a mantle onto the row-4 platform at the top. It's an unusually committed vertical section for a room whose doors are both at floor level.
archetype_guess: side-entry chimney climb with a free-fall return leg (up-and-over corridor)

one_line: A long empty runway ends in a sealed wall you must wall-jump thirteen tiles up a narrow chimney, crest near the ceiling, and then pick your way back down an open east face past a small cluster of hanging spikes to the exit.
structure: West-to-east traversal in three beats: flat run east, vertical 5-tile-wide chimney climb between two full-height walls (cols 12 and 18), then a descending platform staircase down the open east half to the east door. Effectively an up-and-over rather than a corridor.
hazards: Minimal: a single floating bed of four downward spikes at y=11 under the upper east one-way platform, punishing a lazy straight drop. No spikes anywhere in the climb, no timed elements.
distinctive: The room is a disguised wall: a full-height barrier forces a ceiling-height crossover, and the coin sits right at the crest so the "optional" prize is really just the apex of the mandatory route.
archetype_guess: wall-jump chimney crossover with staircase descent
gated wall-jump climb chamber / vertical coin vault
distinctive: A ceiling bed of downward spikes (row 10, cols 18-24) hangs across the tall right-hand bay with only narrow gaps at each side wall, so the climb to coin 51 must be threaded up one edge rather than straight up the middle.
hazards: Single hazard: one horizontal row of downward-pointing spikes forming a partial ceiling mid-bay; no spike floors, no walls of spikes, no timed elements. Punishes drifting toward the centre of the shaft during a wall-jump chain.
one_line: You run east along a low floor corridor, then break upward into a tall pillar-divided chamber and wall-jump a long chain up one side of a spike-fanged ceiling to snag the coin before dropping back to a coin-locked east gate.
structure: Wide room split by three full-height solid pillars (cols 10, 16, 26) into a dead left block, a narrow 5-wide shaft, a tall 9-wide main bay, and a 4-wide right shaft; travel is west-to-east along the open bottom rows with a vertical detour up the main bay. Small sub-floor pockets under the bottom corridor and a couple of one-way platforms (row 15 left, row 15 right, row 7 in the bay).

one_line: A short, mostly flat left-to-right sprint along the bottom strip of a mostly empty room, hopping three beds of floor spikes via a couple of one-way platforms and popping up onto a small ledge stack near the east wall to snag a coin before the exit.
structure: Horizontal corridor, travelling west to east; doors are gaps in both side walls in the lower band (rows 14-17). The upper two-thirds is a large open cavern with scattered floating blocks and two one-way platforms that the route never touches.
hazards: Three short upward-spike beds on the floor row (cols 8-10, 16-19, 25-27) with generous safe gaps between them; no ceiling spikes, no side spikes, no timed elements.
distinctive: The coin-40 detour: a two-tile solid nub at col 25-26 plus the one-way platform at cols 27-29 form a tiny staircase against the east wall column, letting you hop up over the last spike bed to the coin instead of running straight past it.
archetype_guess: spike-floor hop corridor with an optional low-height coin perch

one_line: A calm, hazard-free zig-zag climb: sprint the length of each shelf, then dash-and-wall-kick up through a narrow slot at the alternating end, three times, before stepping out the ceiling hatch.
structure: Vertical switchback ascent: three near-full-width horizontal shelves (rows 6, 10, 14) stacked 4 tiles apart, each with its opening at the opposite end (right, left, right), so travel alternates east-west while the net direction is upward from the bottom corridor to a ceiling exit gap at the top centre.
hazards: None at all — no spikes of any kind anywhere in the grid. The only failure mode is missing a rise and falling back a tier, which costs time rather than a life.
distinctive: Single-tile nubs hanging above each shelf opening (row 5 col 27, row 9 col 4, row 13 col 27) turn each switchback into a tight slot: the 4-tile rise is right at the ceiling of a plain jump, so you must dash into the gap and kick off the end wall to clear the lip. That repeated dash+kick-through-a-letterbox is the room's whole identity.
archetype_guess: switchback lift shaft (alternating-end shelf climb)

one_line: A wide west-to-east dash crossing over a spike bed, hopping off a single tiny mid-air platform, with a tall empty hall above hiding a coin you must wall-climb the right wall to reach.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor traversed west to east across the lower fifth of the room; the upper two-thirds is one large empty vault used only for the optional vertical detour up the east wall.
hazards: A single 13-tile upward spike bed (row 17, cols 10-22) covering the whole floor between the two entry ledges; no spike walls, no timed elements. Failure is a fall into it, not a mistimed hazard.
distinctive: The lone 5-tile one-way platform (row 12) is the only foothold across the spike bed and sits above the ledges, so the crossing is an up-then-down dash rhythm rather than a flat hop; the coin at (264,60) sits ~90px above the east ledge in otherwise wholly empty air, making it a pure wall-jump-chain reward gated on the glove.
archetype_guess: spike-floor gap crossing with a single mid-air stepping stone

one_line: A wide empty spawn hall where you land, stroll right, optionally hop a four-step staircase of floating platforms for the game's first coin, and step out the east door — nothing can go wrong.
structure: A single 32x18 open box, essentially an empty rectangle, with left-to-right travel: solid floor along the bottom, one solid 4x2 block near the right wall acting as a step, and the only exit a 2-tile east door gap at mid-low height. Nine-tenths of the volume (the entire upper two-thirds) is unused air.
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes of any kind, no shutters, no pits. The floor is unbroken wall-to-wall.
distinctive: It is the game's opening screen and the coin-0 platform staircase is a genuinely optional detour off the exit path — the room can be beaten by walking right and never leaving the floor.
archetype_guess: empty walk-through connector / spawn antechamber

one_line: A wide-open east-west transit room whose real content is an optional-feeling but route-critical zigzag dash climb up four staggered one-way platforms to a coin tucked in the top-right corner, with a spike floor waiting for every miss.
structure: Wide 32x18 hall, primary travel west-to-east along the bottom (door gaps in both side walls at rows 14-16); secondary vertical zigzag staircase climbing from the bottom-left platform up-right, back-left, then up-right again to the top-right corner. The middle-left two-thirds of the volume is empty air.
hazards: Two spike beds on the floor (x8-11 and x16-19, upward-facing) covering roughly a quarter of the ground, plus a 5-tile bed of downward spikes hanging at row 7 (x17-21) directly above the mid one-way platform, so the climb has a ceiling threat as well as a floor threat.
distinctive: The overhead spike bed sitting right over the platform you must land on mid-climb: it forces you to land and immediately exit sideways rather than jump straight up, turning a routine platform ladder into a committed direction-reversal.
archetype_guess: dash-chain platform ascent over a spike floor (coin-in-the-corner detour room)

one_line: A left-to-right ground-floor walk where a ten-tile spike bed forces a couple of easy hops across two one-way platforms before you stroll out the east door, with a whole cathedral of unreachable pillars and ledges hanging decoratively overhead.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor, west door to east door, played entirely in the bottom 4 rows (13-16) of an 18-row room; upper 12 rows are open but functionally dead space with hanging pillars (cols 9, 15) and three floating one-way ledges.
hazards: A single upward spike bed on the floor, row 16, columns 17-26. No spike walls, no timing hazards. The west platform strip (cols 3-7) sits over bare floor and guards nothing.
distinctive: The mismatch between the tiny gameplay strip and the elaborate, entirely unreachable upper structure — the room is built like a hall and played like a hallway.
archetype_guess: spike-bed hop corridor (flat transit room)

one_line: A calm, hazard-free junction hall where you either stroll straight through the wide-open bottom corridor or peel off upward and hop a zigzag ladder of one-way platforms to the ceiling exit.
structure: Wide open arena/hall, 32x18. The bottom four rows (14-17) are entirely wall-free, forming a tall west-east through-corridor across the floor. Above it floats a staggered zigzag of one-way platforms — left low (r15 c4-9), centre (r12 c12-18), right (r9 c21-26), back left-centre (r7 c14-18), then directly above (r4 c14-18) — leading to a 4-tile ceiling gap at c14-17. A second one-way at r15 c25-29 is decorative/off-route. Travel is west-east horizontally and a switchbacking ascent vertically.
hazards: None whatsoever. No spikes, no pits, no shutters, no timing elements. Failure means falling back to the floor and re-climbing, never death.
distinctive: The bottom band has no side walls at all — the west and east doors are a full four tiles tall — so the "room" reads as an open gallery you pass through, with the climb sitting overhead as an optional branch to the Watchpost above.
archetype_guess: three-way junction hall with a one-way-platform zigzag ascent

one_line: A left-to-right room whose only path is a narrow 4-tile chimney whose two walls are spiked in alternating vertical bands, so the ascent is a forced rhythm of switching wall-jump sides at exactly the right heights, followed by a relaxed run east along the ceiling gallery and a free drop to the exit.
structure: Three-beat left-to-right room: enter west into a low open floor chamber (cols 0-15, rows 14-16), climb the vertical shaft between the col-12 pillar and the col-17 wall (cols 13-16, rows 5-13), exit over the top into an open upper band (rows 2-3) that runs east, then descend the tall right-hand chamber (cols 18-30) past one-way platforms at row 15 to the east door. Net travel east, with a big U-shaped up-over-down detour.
hazards: Two facing spike walls only, arranged in interlocking bands: right-facing spikes on the left wall at rows 5-7 and 11-13, left-facing spikes on the right wall at rows 8-10 and 14-16. No floor spikes, no ceiling spikes, no timed elements. The spikes never block progress outright; they dictate which wall is legal to touch at each altitude.
distinctive: The alternating spike banding turns a generic chimney into a read-ahead puzzle: you cannot spam one wall or ping-pong freely, you must grip left-clean/right-clean/left-clean in sequence, and the band boundaries fall roughly one jump-rise apart so each transition is a committed swap rather than a recovery.
archetype_guess: spike-banded wall-jump chimney (mandatory vertical gate on a horizontal route)

one_line: A dead-end cul-de-sac entered from below: you pop up through a one-way platform, then wall-jump/dash your way up a tall right-hand chamber over two sparse ledges to snag coin 46, and drop back down carefully because a spike bed sits right beside the exit hole.
structure: Dead-end pocket, ~15 tiles wide of usable space, travelled up-and-back-down. Entry is a floor door (cols 14-17 of the bottom wall) with a one-way platform directly over it. A full-height wall at col 17 splits the room: to its right is a tall open chamber (cols 18-30, 16 tiles high) with two widely spaced one-way ledges (row 12 and row 4); to its left is a narrow blind shaft (cols 11-16) walled by a pillar at col 10, holding a single platform at row 8 and nothing else. Only one door, so the route is a there-and-back.
hazards: One up-facing spike bed on the floor at cols 23-26, sitting between the coin column and the exit — the only hazard. It punishes a sloppy descent from the upper ledge rather than gating the climb itself.
distinctive: The 8-tile (~80px) gap between the two ledges, which forces a wall-jump chain up the central col-17 wall face — no single jump or dash covers it. The lower-left shaft is dead space with no reward or exit.
archetype_guess: floor-entry dead-end coin niche (vertical climb-and-return cache)

one_line: You skip across a spiked floor between two side doors, then peel off upward through a loose ladder of scattered one-way platforms toward a ceiling hatch, drifting sideways each hop to line up the next plank.
structure: Wide open 32x18 shaft with a T-junction plan: flat floor corridor running west-to-east at the bottom (doors in both side walls at row 14), plus a vertical ascent up the middle-left of the chamber to a ceiling gap at columns 14-17. Very little solid geometry — just a spread of short one-way planks stacked at rows 15, 12, 9, 7, 4.
hazards: Two short upward spike beds embedded in the floor surface (cols 10-12 and 20-22), each 3 tiles wide. They only threaten the horizontal transit and any missed landing off the low planks; no walls, ceilings, or moving hazards.
distinctive: It is a genuine three-way hub (west, east, ceiling) whose upward route is optional — the same floor doubles as a fast east-west sprint and as the launch pad for a staggered platform climb, so the room reads differently depending on which exit you want.
archetype_guess: junction hub with one-way-platform ascent over a spiked floor

one_line: A near-empty east-west transit room split by a full-height wall, where the only way through is a floor-level crawl-gap guarded by a two-tile spike patch, with an optional four-step platform staircase on the far side to reach the coin.
structure: Horizontal corridor, west-to-east. A solid wall at column 20 spans rows 2-13, leaving only rows 14-17 open as a low gap at the bottom — everything above is two disconnected empty chambers. West chamber is a bare floor with one cosmetic one-way platform (row 15, cols 5-10). East chamber is a tall empty volume with three staggered one-way platforms (row 16 cols 21-25, row 15 cols 26-29, row 12 cols 21-26) forming a short ascent to a coin hanging at row 9. Doors are floor-level gaps in both side walls (rows 14-16).
hazards: A single upward spike bed of two tiles (row 18, cols 18-19) set in the floor directly at the mouth of the low gap. No spike walls, no timed shutters, nothing else in the room.
distinctive: The full-height dividing wall that forces all traversal through a four-tile-high slot at floor level, with the spikes placed exactly where you'd want to land before ducking through — the room's whole identity is that one pinch point.
archetype_guess: low-gap squeeze corridor with a spike-hop pinch and an optional platform-staircase coin alcove

one_line: A long empty drop-in hall that funnels you into one tall spike-lined chimney where the safe wall alternates side every few tiles, climbed once for a single coin and then re-descended the same way.
structure: Dead-end pocket: a wide open left hall (entered from a ceiling gap at cols 14-17, descending via three staggered one-way platforms), a floor run rightward, then a single ~14-tile vertical chimney (cols 22-26) climbed upward, topping out into an open shelf at rows 2-3 that leads to a narrow 2-tile coin alcove at cols 29-30. Travel is down, right, up, then fully back down and out the ceiling.
hazards: Spike walls only, no floor beds and no timed elements. Both chimney walls (col 21 and col 27) carry inward-facing spikes plus a few upward spikes, and the safe segments on the two walls are deliberately offset (left safe ~rows 4-7 and 10-13; right safe ~rows 2-5, 9-10, 15-16), so the wall-jump chain must switch sides at specific heights. The 5-tile (50px) gap means a mistimed jump has no midair recovery beyond a dash.
distinctive: The offset spike pattern that forces the wall-jump chain to alternate walls at scripted heights, turning the climb into a memorized rhythm rather than a free chain.
archetype_guess: alternating-wall spike chimney (dead-end coin vault)

one_line: A short flat west-to-east sprint where you read the rhythm of three full-height timed shutters, wait in narrow safe bays, and commit a dash through each gap while hopping small spike beds on the floor.
structure: Single-screen horizontal corridor travelled left to right; west and east doors are 4-tile-tall gaps (rows 14-17), and the entire upper 12 rows of the 32x18 box are unused empty air, so play is confined to a thin strip along the floor.
hazards: Tile grid carries only three short floor spike beds (cols 4-7, 14-16, 21-23) plus one pair of downward ceiling spikes near mid-room. The real hazard is code-side: three timed shutters (52px wide, full 170px height, period 96 ticks, active 70, phases 45/13/77) at x=52/134/216, staggered west-to-east, with roughly 3-tile safe bays between them.
distinctive: It is the only room in the dungeon with timed hazards at all — a pure shutter-timing gauntlet rather than a geometry puzzle — and the staggered phases forbid a blind uninterrupted run: you must stop, read the next gate from the preceding bay, and commit.
archetype_guess: timed-shutter dash gauntlet (horizontal gate corridor)

one_line: A dead-end coin pocket entered from below: you pop up through a one-way platform, clear a four-tile spike bed with a dash or long jump, then hop two staggered ledges up the right-hand shaft to a coin and drop back out the way you came.
structure: Tall dead-end chamber, travel up-then-right-then-up-then-back-down. Entry is a floor gap (cols 14-17) under a one-way platform strip. A full-height pillar at col 9 walls off the left third; a second pillar (col 16, rows 3-13) splits the upper space into a narrow blind duct on the left (with one stray platform at row 8) and the real route, an open shaft on the right (cols 17-30) with ledges at row 12 and row 4.
hazards: A single upward spike bed on the floor, four tiles wide (row 17, cols 22-25), sitting immediately right of the only solid landing ledge. It is exactly one dash-length across, so it reads as a one-shot commitment gate rather than a hazard you thread. No other spikes, no walls of spikes, no timed elements.
distinctive: The col-16 pillar creates a wholly vestigial left-hand duct with a platform in it that leads nowhere — the room's namesake shape is dead space, and the actual play is a short climb happening entirely on the other side of it.
archetype_guess: floor-entry dead-end coin niche (vault/cache/duct family): enter from below, short spike-gated climb, single coin, backtrack out

one_line: A big, mostly empty hall where you enter from either side door, hop a sparse zig-zag of five floating one-way platforms up through a lot of dead air, and pop out the ceiling gap — with a small spike bed on the center floor as the only thing punishing a miss.
structure: Wide open 32x18 arena/junction with three exits: west and east door gaps at mid-height (rows 14-16) and a ceiling gap at cols 14-17. Travel is either straight lateral west<->east across open floor, or an upward staircase: low side platforms (row 15, cols 3-7 and 26-29, mirrored) -> row 12 platform (cols 11-16) -> row 9 platform (cols 21-26) -> row 6 platform (cols 14-18) -> ceiling door. The mirrored low platforms are what give the room its "fork" name; the upper chain zig-zags right then back left.
hazards: A single 4-tile up-spike bed on the floor at cols 14-17, flanked by solid floor blocks; the outer thirds of the floor row are open air down to the bottom wall. No spike walls, no timed elements. The spikes sit directly under the climb line, so a whiffed platform jump near the middle is the only real punish — and the platforms are so far apart horizontally that most misses land you safely on solid ground instead.
distinctive: The left-right mirrored pair of low platforms framing the central spike bed — a visual "fork" that reads as a choice but functionally isn't one, since both sides feed the same upward chain.
archetype_guess: open-air three-door junction with floating-platform ascent

one_line: A dead-end treasure vault you drop into from the ceiling onto a lethal spike floor you can never touch, hopping a sparse ladder of one-way platforms down and across to a coin tucked behind a spike sandwich, then climbing all the way back out the same hole.
structure: Wide 32x18 open box entered through a ceiling gap (cols 14-17) with no other exit — an in-and-out dead-end. A solid pillar (col 20, rows 6-12) splits the upper half into left and right chambers; the only crossing is low, under the pillar's base through rows 13-16, because the high crossing is sealed. Traversal is a counter-clockwise loop: fall left, descend to the low platforms, cross right, climb the right chamber, take the coin, then re-cross and climb back to the ceiling.
hazards: Two uses. (1) The entire floor row is up-spikes wall-to-wall — there is no safe ground anywhere in the room, so every landing must be on a one-way platform and a missed jump is death rather than a retry. (2) A spike sandwich across the top-right (up-spikes on row 4 directly over down-spikes on row 5, cols 18-25) seals the high route over the pillar, forcing the low crossing. No timed or moving hazards.
distinctive: The floorless design: a room with zero safe ground where the sparse one-way platforms are the only real geometry, combined with a double-sided spike band that exists purely to forbid the obvious shortcut over the divider.
archetype_guess: lethal-floor platform-hop vault (dead-end coin room, same-door in/out)

one_line: A relaxed west-to-east stroll where you hop a short staircase of one-way platforms over a single floor-to-ceiling pillar, with a two-hop detour up to a coin tucked under an overhanging slab — no danger anywhere.
movement_verbs: short precise landing on pillar top
structure: Wide horizontal corridor traversed west→east (door gaps in both side walls at y=13), bisected by a 2-tile-wide pillar (x15-16) running from the floor up to y=12; staggered one-way platforms form a low staircase up the left side and back down the right. The upper half of the 32x18 room is entirely empty air except one solid slab (x13-21, y7-8).
hazards: None at all — no spikes, no timed elements, no pits. Failure means at worst re-doing a small hop.
distinctive: The central pillar as the room's only real obstacle, plus the single coin (tile ~17,9) hanging in open air directly beneath the ceiling slab, reached by a one-jump detour from the topmost platform.
archetype_guess: hazard-free connective platform-staircase corridor (breather room)

one_line: A dead-end spike belfry you enter through the floor, thread upward between two inward-facing walls of needles to snatch a single coin off the top ledge, then retrace the same thin gaps back down to the only door.
structure: Tall single-chamber shaft, 32x18, travelled up-then-back-down through the same floor gap (x=14-17). The interior is split by a solid pillar at x=11 (rows 5-13) into a narrow left chimney and a wider right ascent; the right side is a two-rung one-way-platform ladder (row 13 and row 7, x=17-22) climbing to a ceiling ledge (row 3-4, x=17-22) where the coin sits at the top-centre.
hazards: Two facing spike walls dominate: a right-pointing column at x=8 running rows 5-15, and a left-pointing column at x=23 running rows 4-13, plus stray spikes at x=11 row 10 and x=14 rows 12-13. No timed elements, no floor spike beds — every hazard is a vertical wall you brush past, so danger comes from horizontal overshoot, not from landing.
distinctive: The one-way platforms dead-end directly into the left-pointing spike wall at x=23, so each hop up must be braked mid-platform rather than carried to the edge — the room punishes momentum instead of imprecision.
archetype_guess: spike-lined vertical shaft / dead-end coin belfry

one_line: You skip east along a low floor past a couple of stub pillars, then zig-zag up a staircase of one-way platforms on the right wall to snag a coin near the ceiling — while a tight, spike-lined chimney on the left glares at you from a part of the room you never actually have to enter.
movement_verbs: wall-jump chain (optional, in the spike chute)
structure: Wide single-screen hall, travel west-to-east along the bottom (both doors are tall bottom-corner gaps, rows 14-17). Two distinct sub-spaces: a narrow 4-tile-wide vertical chute on the left between pillars at col 10 and col 16 (rows 9-13), and an open right half whose only structure is five short one-way platforms staggered two rows apart, forming a left-right zig-zag ladder up to a wide ledge at row 8.
hazards: Spikes only, and only inside the left chute: two right-facing spikes on the left pillar (rows 9-10) and two left-facing spikes on the right pillar (rows 11-12) — an offset "needle" gauntlet punishing a sloppy wall-jump chain. The entire east half and the traversal floor are hazard-free. No timed elements.
distinctive: The offset facing-spike chimney is the room's namesake and its only real teeth — but it is off the critical path and leads nowhere (it opens into empty air at row 8), so the danger is entirely optional flavour while the actual play is a gentle platform staircase.
archetype_guess: staggered one-way-platform ascent with an adjacent optional spike chimney

one_line: A tense alternating-face spike chimney: you wall-jump ~160px up a 4-tile-wide shaft whose left and right walls trade off between safe stone and outward-facing spikes, then pop out into a top corridor and dash a gap over a spike-lined pit to snag the coin — before doing it all again in reverse to leave.
structure: Vertical chimney (cols 14-17) climbed from a floor door at the bottom, opening at the top into a short left-to-right corridor along rows 2-3 over a spike-floored right-hand chamber. It is a dead end — the floor door to GravityLift is the only connection — so the room is an up-and-back-down detour. Roughly a third of the grid (the sealed 11-wide left chamber, cols 1-11) is inert dead space the player can never enter.
hazards: Spike walls are the core: the shaft's left face (col 13) and right face (col 18) alternate in bands of 2-3 tiles between solid stone and inward-pointing spikes, and the bands are offset so exactly one wall is safe at each height. The right chamber's whole floor (row 17, cols 20-30) is upward spikes, punishing any fall from the top corridor. No timed or moving hazards.
distinctive: The offset spike banding that forces the wall-jump chain to alternate sides on a fixed rhythm — the climb reads as a puzzle with one correct cadence rather than free wall-jumping.
archetype_guess: alternating-face spike chimney (dead-end coin niche)

one_line: You enter at the bottom-left, sprint right into a narrow spike-lined chimney and wall-jump up it choosing safe faces, pop out into an attic corridor above the room's own ceiling, dash across two holes in that ceiling to grab the coin perched at the top-left, then return and take a clean vertical drop shaft down the far east wall to the exit.
structure: Three-stage loop over a 32x18 room: a low entry corridor running west-to-east along the floor, a tight vertical spiked chimney (cols ~22-25) climbing the full height on the right-centre, a horizontal attic corridor (rows 1-2) running back east-to-west above the main chamber's roof, and a separate clean drop shaft (cols 28-30) on the far east returning to the east door at row 14. Net travel: up, back left, then straight down.
hazards: Heavy and structural. A full-width up-spike bed (row 8, cols 1-20) is the floor of the big upper chamber, so any fall from the attic through a roof gap that misses the small mid-air ledge (row 7, cols 10-12) kills. The climbing chimney is spiked on its left face for four consecutive rows (right-pointing spikes, rows 10-13) plus a left-pointing spike on the opposite face at row 13 and again at row 7, creating a pinch where both walls are momentarily hostile, and an up-spike at its base (row 14). No timed elements — all static geometry you must read.
distinctive: The coin sits on top of the room: you climb past the playable chamber entirely and traverse an attic corridor whose floor is the chamber's own ceiling, dashing over two gaps that would drop you onto the spike bed. Reading the room from above, with the earlier space visible below as a hazard, is a genuinely novel framing, and the east drop shaft gives the loop a clean, non-repetitive return leg.
archetype_guess: spiked wall-jump chimney into an over-the-roof dash traverse (climb-and-return coin loop)

one_line: You walk west-to-east along an empty floor while a decorative staircase of one-way platforms floats overhead leading nowhere.
structure: Wide open 32x18 hall, horizontal west-to-east travel; both doors are low (rows 14-17, floor level) so the critical path is a flat ground run. A loose zig-zag of short one-way platforms (rows 13, 10, 7, 4, alternating left-of-centre and right-of-centre) climbs toward the ceiling, plus two low platforms at row 15 flanking the doorways, but the ceiling is solid — the "lift" ascent is a dead end.
hazards: None. No spikes of any kind, no shutters, nothing that can kill you.
distinctive: The vertical ladder of platforms implies a lift shaft you're meant to ride, but there is no ceiling exit and no pickup up there, so the room's only real content is a flat walk underneath its own scenery.
archetype_guess: empty transit hall / flat side-door connector with ornamental platforms

one_line: You walk in from one side of a wide-open box, stroll along a flat floor past two lone decorative spikes, and either keep walking out the other side or step onto a one-way slot and drop through — no jump, no hazard, no decision that costs anything.
structure: Three-way horizontal hub: a full-width walkable floor band (rows 13-16) with west and east door gaps at the same height and a 4-tile drop-through slot in the floor at columns 14-17 leading down to Moon Vault. Roughly the top two-thirds of the 32x18 grid is empty air with scattered, unreachable-and-unneeded one-way platform strips and a ceiling spike row.
hazards: Effectively none in the played space. Two isolated up-spikes at row 15 (cols 11 and 20) sit beside the floor line and can be walked around without slowing down; the vvvvv down-spikes and vv pair high in the room decorate airspace the player never enters.
distinctive: Nothing — it is a flat crossroads whose entire built vocabulary (upper platform strips, ceiling spikes) is scenery; the only real content is choosing a door.
archetype_guess: flat junction / routing hub with decorative spikes

one_line: A short, breezy west-to-east ground run where you hop three evenly spaced spike triplets on the floor and step up onto a one-way platform to reach the east door, with a large empty upper half you never touch.
structure: Horizontal corridor, west to east, played almost entirely in the bottom four rows; the upper two-thirds of the 32x18 box is empty air with a couple of stray one-way platforms the route never needs.
hazards: Floor spikes only in practice: three up-spike triplets on the bottom row (~x=8-10, 15-17, 22-24) separated by safe gaps wide enough to land in. A band of nine down-pointing ceiling spikes sits ~10 tiles above the play line and is effectively decorative. No timed shutters, no spike walls.
distinctive: Almost nothing; the only character is the metronomic rhythm of three equal spike triplets with a one-way platform offset above, which half-justifies the "piston" name. No coins, no pickups, just west/east doors.
archetype_guess: spike-floor hop corridor (flat east-west traverse)
three-door hub / drop-through fork room
distinctive: The upper two-thirds of the room is empty air with three orphaned one-way platforms and a 4-tile down-spike cluster no route ever passes near — all the actual play happens in the bottom four rows.
hazards: Essentially none in practice: a single bed of four down-pointing ceiling spikes (row 6, cols 19-22) floats in dead space well away from any platform you'd use. No spike walls, no timed shutters. Only real failure is the open floor gap, which is itself a door.
one_line: You walk in from the side into a cavernous mostly-empty chamber, take two easy hops along low one-way ledges to the middle, and drop through a platform into the floor door — over in about four seconds with nothing asked of you.
structure: Wide horizontal hub, travel primarily west-to-east along the bottom with a downward branch: side doors are gaps in both walls at row 14, and a floor gap (cols 14-17) sits under a solid shelf whose centre is one-way platform.
