The lower band (rows 15-18) is a shallow stepped basin; rows 1-13 are a tall empty void with three isolated floating one-way ledges.

one_line: A left-to-right dash-and-hop climb: you leap from one tiny one-way platform to the next up a rising diagonal, tag a coin tucked under the ceiling on the right, then drop back to the east door.
structure: Wide open horizontal hall (32x18) travelled west-to-east; doors are three-tile gaps in both side walls at the bottom (rows 14-16). The interior is mostly empty air with four small one-way platforms forming an ascending staircase from low-left to high-right, plus a landing pad beside the east door.
hazards: Spike beds cover most of the floor (three up-spike clusters at cols 7-10, 14-17, 21-24), so a missed platform kills. A band of down-spikes on the ceiling (cols 15-23) caps the middle of the ascent and punishes over-jumping.
distinctive: The ceiling down-spikes sit directly above the mid-climb platforms, squeezing the ascent into a height-limited channel; the coin (dungeon-coin-41) sits high and right, just past the end of that spike band.
archetype_guess: spike-floor platform-hop corridor (ascending staircase variant)

one_line: A quick, low-stakes east-west skip along the bottom fifth of an otherwise empty hall: two spike beds on the ground force you onto three one-way platforms, and the only moment of tension is a short pop off the centre platform to grab a coin tucked just under an overhead spike ceiling.
movement_verbs: short vertical hop under ceiling spikes
structure: Wide horizontal corridor traversed west-to-east (both side walls open across the lower four rows). All playable content is compressed into the bottom 4-5 rows: left one-way platform (cols 3-8, row 15), centre one-way platform raised one tile (cols 14-17, row 14), right one-way platform (cols 23-29, row 15), with solid floor below. The top ~11 rows are completely empty dead space.
hazards: Two up-spike beds on the floor (cols 9-13 and 18-22) sitting exactly under the gaps between platforms, so the ground route is punished and the platform route is the intended line. One 10-tile down-spike band floating at row 9 far overhead; it is out of reach from the floor and only matters as a ceiling on the jump from the centre platform, where the coin sits ~2 tiles up. No timed or moving hazards.
distinctive: The floating down-spike band acting as a low ceiling over the coin hop off the centre platform — a single "jump, but not too high" beat. Everything else is stock.
archetype_guess: spike-bed hop corridor with staggered one-way platforms (flat horizontal connector room)

one_line: A quiet, hazard-free dead-end cache: you pop up through the floor door, cross right, and climb a two-tier stack of long wooden rafters (with a wall-jump off the central pillar to reach the first one) to snag coin 20 in the top-right corner, then drop straight back out the way you came.
structure: Dead-end chamber entered from below (only door is "floor", cols 14-17); a short one-way lip above the door leads right into a tall vertical shaft (cols 17-30) bounded left by a solid pillar at col 16, with two long horizontal rafters at row 11 and row 4; travel is up-and-back-down. A second, entirely separate left chamber (cols 1-9) is walled off by the col-10 pillar and reachable only across the open ceiling band — pure dead space.
hazards: None. Zero spikes anywhere in the grid; the only failure is a missed jump costing height, and even that is a soft reset since there is nothing to land on that hurts.
distinctive: The stacked 7-tile one-way rafters read as an actual shrine loft — you pass up through them and can drop back through, so the climb and the exit reuse the same geometry in opposite directions. Less flattering: roughly a third of the room (the whole left chamber and its stub ledge at row 7) is unreachable-by-need scenery you never touch.
archetype_guess: one-way-platform coin cache / dead-end vault loft

one_line: A straight-line west-to-east ground sprint where you clear three identical 40px spike beds with three identical dash-jumps, in a room whose entire upper two-thirds you never touch.
structure: Single-height horizontal corridor along the floor, travelling left to right; doors are edge gaps at rows 14-15 on both the west and east walls, so you enter and exit at the same low level. The room is 18 tiles tall but the playable line occupies only the bottom four rows.
hazards: Three floor-level spike beds (up-spikes) on row 17, each exactly 4 tiles / 40px wide, at x7-10, x14-17 and x21-24, separated by 3-4 tile safe landing strips. A 10-tile band of down-pointing spikes hangs at row 7, roughly 70px above head height on the travel line — pure decoration, never a threat. No shutters, no timing elements.
distinctive: The spike beds are all the same width with the same gaps, so the room is one dash-jump repeated three times with no escalation, variation or choice; the four scattered one-way platforms (rows 9, 11, 14, 15) sit off the line and lead nowhere.
archetype_guess: spike-bed dash gauntlet corridor

one_line: You sprint east along an open floor into a dead-end wall, then wall-jump ~13 tiles up a narrow chimney whose two faces are spiked in alternating bands, so every jump must land on the one side that is safe at that height, before topping out and dropping down a wide open right-hand hall onto platforms to the east exit.
structure: Left-to-right corridor entered at the west wall (rows 14-16), blocked by a full-height wall at x=16; a 4-5 tile wide vertical chimney between the x=10 pillar and that wall carries you up ~13 tiles to an open ceiling band (rows 1-3), which you cross east and then descend through a large empty right-hand hall to the east door at rows 14-16, cushioned by a one-way platform run at x=24-29.
hazards: Only spike walls, no floors or timed elements: right-facing spikes on the chimney's left face at rows 4-6 and 11-13, left-facing spikes on its right face at rows 7-10 and 14-16, deliberately interleaved so the safe grab side flips twice during the climb.
distinctive: The spike bands on the two chimney faces are offset rather than mirrored, turning the climb into a read-ahead puzzle about which wall to be on at each height instead of a pure wall-jump chain.
archetype_guess: alternating-face spiked wall-jump chimney (shared with nova-niche, zenith-shaft, lattice-climb)

one_line: A flat left-to-right sprint across three one-way platforms, dash-jumping twice over identical six-tile spike beds, under an enormous empty void of unused air.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor, west-to-east, with all play compressed into the bottom four rows: door gaps at row 14 in both side walls, a one-way platform strip at row 15 broken into three segments (cols 3-9, 16-19, 26-29), spikes at row 17, solid floor at row 18. Rows 1-13 are completely empty air the player never touches.
hazards: Two up-spike beds on the floor (cols 10-15 and 20-25), directly under the two platform gaps. Pure fall-punishment for a missed dash-jump; no timed, moving, wall, or ceiling hazards.
distinctive: Almost nothing: the two crossings are the same 6-tile gap over the same 6-tile spike bed twice in a row, and the middle platform is only 4 tiles wide so a fast landing can skid you into the second pit. No coins or pickups. The 13 rows of empty sky read as a design void rather than a feature.
archetype_guess: flat spike-pit dash-gap corridor

one_line: A flat left-to-right sprint where you dash or jump over three identical three-tile spike beds with generous flat landings between them, and never once look up.
structure: Single-lane horizontal corridor, west door to east door, played entirely in the bottom three rows; the upper two-thirds of the 32x18 grid is empty air with three stranded one-way platforms (rows 6, 9, 12) that no route ever touches.
hazards: Three upward spike beds on the floor (cols 8-10, 15-17, 22-24), each 3 tiles / 30px wide, separated by 4-tile flat safe ground. No ceiling spikes, no walls, no timing elements — every hazard is static and identically sized.
distinctive: Nothing — the only mild texture is the short one-way platform strips at the two door mouths (cols 3-7 and 27-29), which change nothing about how you cross.
archetype_guess: flat spike-bed hop/dash corridor

one_line: You drop through the ceiling into a wide empty cellar, stroll left to scoop two coins off the floor, then hop back up a generously spaced zigzag ladder of one-way platforms and leave the way you came.
structure: Single 32x18 chamber, dead-end. The only opening is a 4-tile ceiling gap at cols 14-17 (to/from Split Root), so travel is down-then-back-up the same shaft. Interior is a staggered stack of one-way platforms alternating left (cols 8-13) and right (cols 14-19) every 2 rows from row 14 up to row 4, plus a long left ledge at rows 14-15. Vertical gaps are ~20px against a ~40px jump rise, so every hop has huge margin.
hazards: One vestigial 2-tile up-spike bed on the floor at cols 5-6 (row 17), positioned away from both coins and the climb; it can be walked around without thought. Effectively hazard-free.
distinctive: Nothing — it is an unguarded coin cache (coins 2 and 3 at x=20, y=126/158 on the left floor/ledge) whose built platform ladder the coins never force you to use.
archetype_guess: dead-end coin-cache chamber with a zigzag one-way-platform climb

one_line: You pop up through a one-way floor hatch into a big empty right-hand box, walk left, then thread a tall spike-lined chimney whose safe wall alternates sides every three tiles, grab the coin on the top ledge, and free-fall back down onto the platforms while dodging the spike floor.
structure: Two-part dead-end: a wide open ~16x15 chamber on the right (entered from a floor door at cols 14-17 via one-way platforms), and a narrow 3-tile-wide vertical chimney on the left (cols 6-8, rows 2-16) that is the only way up. Travel is up the left chimney, right along the top corridor to the coin, then a straight fall back down the right chamber to the same floor door. Out-and-back, no through-route.
hazards: Dense spike walls define the chimney: right-facing spikes on col 5 (rows 2-4, 8-10, 14-15) and left-facing spikes on col 9 (rows 6-7, 11-13), arranged so the safe wall alternates left/right in ~3-tile bands — you cannot chain wall-jumps on one side. Plus an 11-tile up-spike bed on the chamber floor (row 17, cols 20-30) that punishes a lazy descent. No timed/moving hazards.
distinctive: The alternating spike-banding of the chimney: safe purchase swaps walls every three rows, forcing a rhythmic left-right wall-jump chain up ~110px rather than a single-wall grind.
archetype_guess: spike-lined wall-jump chimney + open drop-back cache room

one_line: A ceiling-entry dead-end vault: you drop down a narrow chute with spikes lining its right wall, duck under a pillar into a bright right-hand chamber, hop two one-way ledges up to coin 42 near the ceiling, then have to climb the spiked chute back out the way you came.
structure: Single-entry dead-end pocket entered from a ceiling gap (cols 14-17). Two full-height pillars (col 10 rows 5-17, col 17 rows 3-13) split the 32x18 box into three: a large empty left pocket (cols 1-9, only reachable over the col-10 pillar top), a narrow vertical descent chute (cols 11-16) under the entrance, and an open right chamber (cols 18-30) with a stacked pair of one-way ledges (row 13 cols 18-22, row 5 cols 18-23). Travel is down-then-right-then-up, and the return is the exact reverse — an out-and-back, not a through-route.
hazards: One short spike wall only: three left-facing spikes at col 16, rows 9-11, set into the left face of the right pillar so they bite into the descent chute. They force the fall to hug the left (col-10) wall and, more painfully, constrain the wall-jump chain on the way back up. No spike beds, no timed elements.
distinctive: The chute is entrance and exit both, so the spikes are paid for twice with different demands: descending you just steer away from them, ascending you must wall-jump up a 6-tile-wide slot whose right wall is lethal for three tiles, using the row-9 one-way as the only rest. The coin (col 22, row 3) is also teasingly near the ceiling you entered through but walled off from it by the col-17 pillar.
archetype_guess: dead-end ceiling-drop treasure vault with a spiked re-ascent chute

one_line: A west-to-east traverse over a near-continuous spike floor where you first wall-jump a three-tile chute up a full-height pillar and run its roof, then immediately dive back under a hanging mast to snake into the open eastern chamber and grab the coin off a suspended platform.
structure: Horizontal west-to-east corridor at rows 14-16 interrupted by a vertical detour: entry (west door rows 14-16) → one-way platform run cols 5-10 → narrow 3-tile chute between the col-7 stub and the full-height col-11 pillar (rows 6-16) → over the pillar top and east along the row-6 shelf (cols 11-17) → forced descent in the cols 18-19 slot to pass beneath the ceiling-hung mast at col 20 (rows 2-10) → open eastern chamber (cols 21-30) with a floating roof at row 14 (cols 21-27) holding coin 62 above it → drop off its east lip and out the east door. Up-then-across-then-down profile; net travel eastward.
hazards: One long bed of upward spikes covering essentially the whole floor (row 17, cols 6-28), leaving only a five-tile safe ledge at the far west and a three-tile ledge at the far east. No spike walls, no timed elements — every mistake is the same failure: a fall onto the floor. That makes the whole room a no-touch-down traverse rather than a puzzle of reading which surface is safe.
distinctive: The over-then-under beat: the pillar forces you high, and the ceiling-hung mast immediately forces you back low through a two-tile slot, so the "bridge" you build across the spikes has to change altitude mid-crossing instead of being one flat run.
archetype_guess: spike-floor traverse with a vertical wall-jump detour ("bridge over a pit" family, with a ceiling-obstacle twist)

one_line: A short, flat west-to-east sprint along the floor where you hop three evenly spaced spike beds in a rhythm, under a big empty hall whose upper platforms you never touch.
structure: Wide horizontal corridor, travelling east (or west on the return); all real play happens on the bottom two rows, with the top ~11 rows an unused open hall containing three isolated 3-tile platforms in an ascending staircase.
hazards: Three 4-tile (40px) upward spike beds set into the floor at cols 7-10, 14-17, 21-24, separated by 3-4 tile safe gaps. No spike walls, no ceiling spikes, no timed elements.
distinctive: The metronomic evenness: three identical spike beds at identical spacing, so the room is one jump input repeated three times. Its only other feature — the staircase of platforms at rows 12/9/6 — sits 50px+ above the floor with no wall-jump surfaces or lower steps to reach it, so it is effectively unreachable scenery rather than an optional high line.
archetype_guess: spike-floor hop corridor (flat side-scrolling connector)

one_line: A wide, mostly empty flat hall you jog straight through west-to-east, hopping one small three-tile spike strip and a couple of decorative one-way ledges before reaching a coin-gated door.
structure: Single-storey horizontal corridor, west-to-east travel: tall 3-tile door gaps in both side walls at rows 14-16, a continuous solid floor along the bottom, and roughly 11 rows of entirely unused dead air above.
hazards: One 3-tile spike bed (up-facing, cols 11-13) sitting on the floor mid-room; 30px wide against a 40px jump, so it is cleared by a casual jump. No other hazards, no shutters, no walls of spikes.
distinctive: Its east door is the coin-gated entrance to the glove region (DEMO_DUNGEON_GLOVE_GATE_REQUIREMENT) — the gate, not the geometry, is the only thing that makes this room matter.
archetype_guess: flat spike-hop transit corridor / gate antechamber

one_line: A dead-end detour room entered from below: you pop up through one-way platforms, hop a short spike bed to the right, then wall-jump up a tall pillar past two thin ledges to snatch coin 34 near the ceiling and drop back out the way you came.
structure: Single-door pocket: the only opening is a 4-tile floor gap at bottom-centre (to Lift Shaft), so travel is up-and-back. A full-height pillar at column 16 splits the space; the right half is a ~15-tile shaft with two 5-6 tile one-way ledges (row 12 and row 4) staggered off the pillar's right face, and the coin sits above the upper ledge. The left third is a tall sealed pocket behind another pillar (col 9) with a single platform, essentially unused dead space.
hazards: One small upward spike bed (3 tiles, ~30px) on the right-hand floor between the entrance platforms and the base of the climb — clearable with a running jump or dash. No spike walls, no timed elements. Falling off the upper ledges costs only re-climb time, not death, unless you land on the spikes.
distinctive: The 5-tile (50px) gap from floor to the first ledge is deliberately above jump height, so the pillar face forces a genuine wall-jump chain rather than a stair-step climb; the coin is placed one tile past the ledge edge so the last hop is a committed reach.
archetype_guess: dead-end coin alcove / wall-jump ascent side room

one_line: You walk in one side door, jog across a flat floor, and either walk out the far side or step through a one-way slot in the middle of the floor — almost nothing resists you.
structure: Wide 32x18 horizontal hall with a solid floor along the bottom and three-tile door bands cut into both side walls (rows 14-16), plus a downward branch through a 4-tile one-way slot at mid-floor. Travel is straight west-east, with an optional vertical exit. The upper two-thirds is empty air.
hazards: Two up-spikes on the floor row flanking the central solid block, and a 4-tile down-spike cluster hanging near the ceiling that no route ever approaches. Effectively zero hazard pressure; the floor spikes are not close enough to the one-way lips to make committing to the descent feel like a decision.
distinctive: Nothing meaningful — the one-way floor slot is the only structural idea and it costs no skill to use; the ceiling spikes and the three stacked mid-air platforms (rows 9, 11, 13) are pure decoration on a route nobody flies. No coins or pickups in the room.
archetype_guess: flat-floor three-way junction room (Split Root / Cullet Fork / Pressure Fork family)

one_line: A wide, almost empty hall you jog straight across at floor level, stepping over two token spike pips on each side, with the only real decision being whether to drop through the central one-way platform into Shard Vault.
structure: Wide horizontal 3-way junction: west door (rows 14-16) to east door (rows 14-16) along a single floor lane on row 17, plus a floor door straight down through a 4-tile one-way platform at the horizontal centre. The upper two-thirds of the room is open air containing a symmetric lattice of one-way platforms that no route uses.
hazards: Four single up-spike pips embedded in the floor in mirrored `^#^` pairs (cols 9/11 and 20/22), trivially stepped over at running speed; a 5-tile down-spike cluster near the ceiling (row 6) that is decoration only, far above anything reachable. No timed elements, no spike walls.
distinctive: Its perfect left-right mirror symmetry around the central drop slot — the room reads as a signpost rather than a challenge, and its whole built structure (platform lattice, ceiling spikes) is inert.
archetype_guess: decorative symmetric 3-way junction hall (walk-through fork with drop slot)

one_line: A three-second walk across a flat shelf near the floor of a mostly-empty box: step in from the west, hop one lone spike, and either keep walking east or tap down through the one-way slot to the Root Cellar.
structure: Wide horizontal junction, travelled left-to-right along the bottom four rows of a 32x18 box; west and east doors sit at the same height (rows 14-15) with a third exit straight down through a 4-tile one-way slot in the floor at cols 14-17. The upper two-thirds of the room (rows 1-13) is entirely empty air with one unreachable decorative platform at row 12.
hazards: Two single up-spikes on row 16 (cols 12 and 19), one flanking each side of the central ####----#### block. Both are trivially cleared by a normal jump and neither guards anything; there are no spike walls, no timed elements, and effectively no death risk.
distinctive: The floor-drop slot to the Root Cellar is the only real feature — this is the game's first branching choice (room 3) — but nothing makes the choice cost anything.
archetype_guess: flat three-way junction with drop-through floor slot

one_line: A calm three-lane junction room: you walk in low from the west, chimney up a narrow one-way-assisted shaft between two tall pillars, and then either pop out the ceiling door or vault over the right-hand pillar and pick your way down a staggered platform staircase to the east exit.
structure: Wide hall split by two full-height pillars (col 12, rows 3-13; col 18, rows 6-16) into three vertical lanes. Travel is west→up→(ceiling exit) or west→up→over the top→east→down. Lane 1 (cols 1-11) is an open entry corridor along the bottom; lane 2 (cols 13-17) is a 5-tile-wide chimney with two offset one-way platforms (row 7 left, row 4 right) leading to the ceiling gap at cols 14-17; lane 3 (cols 19-30) is a descending slalom of six short one-way ledges plus one long shelf (row 10) down to the east door at rows 14-16.
hazards: None at all — no spikes anywhere. All difficulty is geometry and fall-recovery; a missed climb just costs you a re-run up the chimney.
distinctive: The right-hand pillar seals rows 6-16, so the east route is only reachable by climbing the central chimney to near the ceiling and crossing right along the open roof band — the room forces the vertical detour before it lets you continue horizontally, and the ceiling door sits right where that climb tops out, making the ascent do double duty as the fork.
archetype_guess: hub fork / wall-jump chimney with branching one-way descent

one_line: A lazy zigzag climb up staggered one-way platforms on the east side, capped by a coin grab at the summit, then a tense controlled descent down a narrow chimney whose two walls alternate spike beds so you must keep swapping which side is safe.
structure: Two-part room, travel east-to-west (reversible). East two-thirds is a tall open hall (cols 13-30) with six one-way platforms staggered left/right every 2 rows, forming an ascending switchback ladder from the east door (rows 14-17) to the ceiling. At the top you traverse left over a solid shelf (row 4, cols 11-17) past coin 52 (col ~14, rows 2-3), then enter a 4-tile-wide vertical chimney (cols 7-10) running the full height down to the bottom, which spills west onto a small ledge and the west door (rows 14-15). A dead-ended 4-wide left corridor (cols 1-4) sits behind the spiked wall and is pure backdrop.
hazards: Spike beds mounted on both chimney walls in alternating vertical bands: right-facing spikes on the left wall at rows 2-3, 8-10, 14-15; left-facing spikes on the right wall at rows 5-6, 11-13. No spikes at all in the east hall; no timed shutters or moving hazards. Clear channel is 40px wide, shrinking to ~30px wherever a band bites in — exactly a dash's width, so a mistimed dash buries you.
distinctive: The alternating spike chimney: safe wall flips three times on the way down, so a wall-jump chain must be deliberately broken and re-established on the opposite face rather than machine-gunned. It also cleanly juxtaposes a relaxed climb against a nervous descent in one room.
archetype_guess: staggered one-way-platform ascent feeding a spiked wall-jump chimney descent

one_line: A left-to-right traverse that funnels you off a solid floor onto a 12-tile spike bed you can only cross by wall-jumping up the face of one pillar, committing to a dash across open air, and catching the far pillar before the spikes catch you.
structure: Wide horizontal traverse west→east across a 32x18 box: a tall empty left shaft (walled by a full-height pillar at col 7 and a second at col 12), then the main event — an open bay whose only floor is spikes, spanned between the right face of the col-12 pillar and the left face of the col-25 pillar — then a short two-tile spike hop to a solid landing and the east door. Vertically it is a shallow chimney-then-gap hybrid rather than a true climb, despite the name.
hazards: One long upward-facing spike bed (cols 13–24, ~120px) forming the entire floor of the central bay, plus a two-tile spike patch (cols 26–27) just past the far pillar. No spike walls, no timed elements — all hazard pressure is a single uninterrupted floor of death you must never touch.
distinctive: The crossing is longer than a single dash (12 tiles vs ~4 tiles of dash), so you must gain height off the col-12 wall first and then spend the dash mid-fall as a committed, unrecoverable reach for the col-25 wall — a "bank altitude, then commit" beat rather than a rhythm chain.
archetype_guess: spike-bed gap crossing / wall-to-wall dash relay

one_line: You pop up through a hole in the floor into a big, empty, hazard-free hall and zig-zag up five widely-staggered one-way platforms to snag coin 26 tucked under the ceiling at top-right, then drop back out the way you came.
structure: A single 30x16 open box, no interior solids except a small floor plinth; the only opening is the 4-tile gap in the bottom wall, so it is a dead-end pocket entered and exited from below. Net travel is up-and-back: bottom-left platform (r15) -> mid-left (r12) -> upper-left (r6) -> right side (r9) -> top-right (r3) -> coin at the ceiling, col ~23.
hazards: None whatsoever. No spikes, no shutters, no pits; a missed jump just dumps you onto the floor for a free retry.
distinctive: It is a cul-de-sac treasure pocket rather than a route room — the same floor gap is both entrance and exit, and the whole space is negative air with five islands hanging in it.
archetype_guess: hazard-free staggered-platform dash climb / coin alcove

one_line: You drop in from the west onto a low ledge, and the room immediately asks a question: hop right along the ground past a short spike bed to the east door, or turn and climb a wide, airy zigzag of one-way platforms up to the ceiling hatch — the traversal is easy either way, the interest is entirely in the choice.
movement_verbs: dash (optional, to shorten the widest platform gap)
structure: Wide open 32x18 hall, effectively empty in the middle, with travel in two directions at once: a flat west-to-east ground corridor along the bottom three rows, and a staircase of four/five one-way platforms zigzagging up-left/up-right from the low-left ledge (row 15) through rows 13, 10, 7 to a final platform at row 4 directly under the ceiling door. Split-path / vertical-branch off a horizontal corridor.
hazards: Minimal: one four-tile upward spike bed on the floor (cols 17-20, row 17) sitting in the middle of the ground route between the west and east doors. Nothing threatens the climb at all — a fall from the top just costs you the re-climb, not a death.
distinctive: The room is a genuine three-door junction (west to Pulse Gallery, east to Relay Chasm, ceiling to the Storm Cache coin room) where the optional coin branch is the vertical one — the climb is visibly a detour off the main horizontal line, so the fork reads instantly without a sign.
archetype_guess: open-hall platform staircase with a side-exit fork (junction room)

one_line: A wide-open east-west floor sprint where you hop two spike beds and snag a coin mid-jump over the second one, while three-quarters of the room's architecture hangs overhead doing nothing.
structure: Left-to-right corridor along the very bottom of a 32x18 room: the west and east door gaps span rows 14-17, so travel is confined to a ~4-tile-tall floor lane. Two one-way platforms (cols 3-7 and cols 23-29 at row 15) act as stepping shelves at either end. Everything above row 13 is a separate, largely vestigial upper hall: a narrow 2-tile wall-jump chimney between the col-2 and col-5 pillars, a solid shelf at row 10 (cols 5-11), a slab at row 11 (cols 17-24), a one-way at row 12 (cols 12-16), and a right-side ledge near col 28 — none of it on the route.
hazards: Two floor spike beds (up-spikes at row 17, cols 8-11 and cols 17-22) forcing two clean jumps; a run of down-spikes at row 8 (cols 14-21) hangs in open air ~6 tiles above the floor and threatens nothing on the main path. No shutters or moving hazards.
distinctive: The coin (200,148) floats directly above the second, wider spike bed, so the one memorable beat is committing to a jump/dash over spikes to collect mid-flight rather than landing safely past them.
archetype_guess: spike-bed hop corridor with a decorative unused upper hall

one_line: You can hold right along an open ground-floor hall and leave in seconds, or detour up a narrow spiked chimney, alternating wall-jumps around spikes that switch walls partway up, to pop out on a rooftop ledge and grab coin 19 before dropping down the open right-hand shaft to the east door.
structure: Wide east-west hall on the bottom band (west door to east door, two small floor pillars to hop), with an upper storey split into three vertical cells by two full-height wall slabs: a large empty left box (cols 1-9, dead space), a 3-tile-wide central chimney (cols 12-14, ~9 tiles tall, entered from below through a one-way platform), and an open right shaft (cols 25-30) that drops back to the hall. A flat roof (row 5, cols 15-24) carries the coin ledge linking chimney top to right shaft. Primary travel is horizontal; the optional detour is a climb-then-descend loop.
hazards: Only spikes, and only inside the chimney: right-facing spikes on the left wall at the upper-middle (rows 6-7) and left-facing spikes on the right wall lower down (rows 9-10). They are offset so you must switch cling walls mid-chain rather than pogo one face — a rhythm/timing gate rather than a damage trap. No timed elements; the whole bottom route is hazard-free.
distinctive: The staggered spike placement in the chimney, forcing an alternating-wall climb whose contact points are dictated rather than free — that plus the fact the entire hazard content is skippable optional coin routing.
archetype_guess: optional spiked-chimney wall-jump detour off a flat transit hall

one_line: A wide, almost entirely empty hall you jog straight through west-to-east in a couple of seconds, with an optional two-hop climb onto a lonely mid-air platform for the coin.
structure: Horizontal corridor, west to east, but only the bottom ~4 rows are used for travel; the upper two-thirds of the 32x18 box is open air with a single floating platform. Door gaps are unusually tall (rows 14-17 on both side walls), so entry and exit are near-floor and very forgiving.
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes, no shutters, no pits. The only failure state is missing a jump and landing harmlessly on the floor.
distinctive: The negative space: roughly 70% of the room is untouched air, and the coin platform (row 12, cols 14-19) floats alone above the two low one-ways, reachable only by a committed running jump from a platform edge. It reads as a deliberate breather/gateway between the Wall Gate wing and the Crossroads hub.
archetype_guess: flat one-way-platform transit hall / breather room with an optional floating-coin perch

one_line: A wide, mostly empty three-way junction where you jog east along an open mid-height band and, if you want the side room, hop down onto a broad spike-flanked one-way platform and drop through the floor slot — a signpost more than a challenge.
structure: 32x18 open arena/hub, primary travel horizontal west-to-east across the unwalled rows 14-16 band, with a secondary vertical branch dropping through a floor slot at cols 14-17 into Lunar Cache. Doors: west (Vacuum Gallery), east (Aurora Spire), floor (Lunar Cache).
hazards: Two spike groups, both effectively decorative. Six down-pointing spikes (row 5, cols 19-24) hang in open air roughly 9 tiles above any surface you'd traverse and are trivially avoided. Two pairs of up-spikes on the floor band (row 17, cols 11-12 and 17-18) flank the one-way drop slot, but the slot's landing platform is 4 tiles wide, so the descent has essentially no precision cost. No timed elements, no shutters.
distinctive: The floor-drop slot is genuinely readable — spikes on both lips visually mark the branch — but the entire upper two-thirds of the room (eight scattered one-way platforms across rows 6-13, plus the ceiling spike cluster) is unreachable-by-need decoration that no route touches and no pickup rewards. The room has no coins at all.
archetype_guess: open-arena three-way fork / hub junction with decorative spike dressing

one_line: A wide open vault where you hop up a zig-zagging staircase of one-way platforms to snag two coins, with a spiked floor making a missed landing a real, if brief, punishment before you drop back out the way you came.
structure: Single 32x18 open arena, essentially empty of solids except four staggered one-way platforms forming an ascending left-to-right-to-left switchback; entry is the west door low on the left wall (rows 14-16), and it is a dead end — you climb up-right for the coins and return to the same door.
hazards: Two short spike beds on the floor (cols 10-12 and 20-22, up-pointing) directly under the climb line; no walls, ceilings, or timed elements. Punishment is positional rather than continuous — the rest of the floor is safe, so a fall usually just costs a re-climb.
distinctive: It is a reward chamber rather than a challenge: two coins (one mid-height at 144,100, one high-right at 244,70) staged as a low-risk victory lap gated behind the Underpass coin requirement (16 coins to open). The airy, mostly-empty volume reads as "vault" and contrasts with the tight corridors that lead here.
archetype_guess: dead-end coin vault / one-way-platform ascent staircase

one_line: A wide, empty hall you can simply stroll through along the bottom west-to-east, unless you want the coin, in which case you hop up a loose zig-zag of one-way platforms to the ceiling exit.
structure: Wide open 32x18 hall: an unobstructed floor corridor (rows 14-17) runs west door to east door, while a sparse staircase of short one-way platforms zig-zags up through the upper 12 rows to a ceiling door at top centre. Horizontal for transit, vertical for the coin.
hazards: None at all — no spikes, no shutters, no moving threats. Failure just means dropping back to the floor and re-climbing, with no cost.
distinctive: Its layered function rather than its geometry: the bottom is a pure pass-through underpass (west door to the Winged Vault, east door to the Treasury, both coin-gated), while coin 13 and the ceiling link up to Wall Gallery live on a separate airy platform ladder overhead. The coin at (224,80) hangs just under the row-7 platform, so it is grabbed on the rise rather than by landing.
archetype_guess: open one-way-platform ascent hub / transit junction

one_line: You cross a big empty west hall to a dead end, then wall-jump up a narrow spike-lined chimney where the safe wall keeps swapping sides, pop over the top, and coast back down a zig-zag of one-way platforms to the east door.
structure: Left-to-right room in three bands: a large open west chamber (cols 1-15) that dead-ends at a full-height pillar; a mandatory 4-tile-wide vertical chimney (cols 12-15) climbed ~14 tiles to the ceiling; then an eastward/downward staircase of alternating one-way platforms (cols 19-27) ending in a narrow outer shaft (cols 29-30) with the east door 3 tiles above the floor. Up-then-over-then-down.
hazards: Spike walls only, and used cleverly: the chimney's left face (col 11, right-pointing) and right face (col 16, left-pointing) are exact complements — at every height exactly one wall is spiked, so the safe wall alternates in blocks of 3-4 tiles. No spike floors, no timed elements. The descent half is completely hazard-free.
distinctive: The perfectly complementary spike faces in the chimney: you can never climb one wall, you must fling across the 40px gap to the opposite wall each time the spikes switch sides — a read-and-commit rhythm rather than a mash-wall-jump climb.
archetype_guess: alternating-face spiked chimney climb with one-way-platform descent

one_line: You enter at floor level on the left, find the way east blocked by a full-height pillar, and have to ladder up a narrow one-way-platform shaft over a small spike bed, tip over the pillar's top, grab a coin tucked in the ceiling on the right, then drop down the open right-hand half to the east door.
structure: Two-chamber room split by a tall solid pillar (col 18, rows 5-17): a west approach at floor level, a ~5-tile-wide vertical shaft between two pillars climbed via staggered one-way platforms (row 7 then row 4), a crossover at the pillar's top, and a large open right chamber you descend through to the east door at floor level. Net travel west-to-east with a mandatory up-and-over.
hazards: One short upward spike bed (3 tiles) on the shaft floor beside the pillar base; nothing else. It only bites if you fall the full height of the climb, and the ladder rungs are wide, so most players never touch it.
distinctive: The up-and-over silhouette: a solid pillar forces a vertical detour in what is otherwise a horizontal transit, and the only real hazard sits directly under the climb.
archetype_guess: one-way-platform ascent shaft with an over-the-wall crossover

one_line: You enter low on the west, jog under a spike-lined chimney, then are forced into a tight alternating wall-jump climb where the safe wall swaps every few tiles, before spilling out onto a relaxed one-way-platform zigzag down to the east door.
structure: Three-part left-to-right room: a flat west approach (cols 1-15, rows 14-17), a narrow ~4-tile-wide vertical chimney between the col-10 pillar and the col-16/17 double pillar that must be climbed the full room height, then a top corridor east and an open east half descended via scattered one-way platforms to the east door at rows 14-15. Net travel is west -> up -> east -> down.
hazards: Spike beds on both chimney walls, banded so they alternate: right-pointing spikes on the left wall at rows 2-3, 8-10 and 14-15; left-pointing spikes on the right wall at rows 5-7 and 11-13. A single downward spike caps the chimney's right lip at the top. All static and readable; no timed elements. East descent is hazard-free.
distinctive: The alternating spike banding turns the chimney into a forced rhythm: only one wall is grabbable at any given height, so the climb is a metronome of side-swapping wall-jumps, and the glove requirement is enforced (a dash-only bypass is proven not to exist by test).
archetype_guess: alternating-spike chimney climb with platform-zigzag descent

one_line: A big, calm, hazard-free hall where you hop up staggered one-way platforms on either side of a lone central pillar and wall-jump its face to pluck a coin from the empty air above it, then drop back down and stroll out the far low door.
structure: Wide open arena (32x18, mostly empty air) with west and east door gaps low on the side walls at rows 14-17, so the through-route is a flat left-right traverse; a single 1-tile-wide solid pillar (col 16, rows 9-15) divides the middle, and two mirrored staircases of 5-tile one-way platforms fan up the left and right halves. The interesting travel direction is the optional vertical detour up the pillar.
hazards: None whatsoever — no spikes, no shutters, no pits. The only failure is missing a wall-jump and falling harmlessly to the floor to retry.
distinctive: The lone central pillar used as a wall-glove tutor: the coin (dungeon-coin-16, ~x161 y50) floats about three tiles above the pillar's top with no platform under it, so it can only be reached by climbing the pillar's face and jumping off the tip — a clean, safe demonstration of the wall-jump in an otherwise consequence-free room.
archetype_guess: hazard-free wide hall with staggered one-way platform stairs plus a single wall-jump pillar — a mechanic-teaching antechamber

one_line: A big airy four-door hub where you zigzag up a staircase of one-way platforms between two tall interior pillars, grabbing a single coin on the way, with nothing anywhere trying to hurt you.
movement_verbs: wall-jump (optional, on the two interior pillars)
dash (required only for the east exit)
structure: 32x18 open chamber acting as a 4-way hub: doors on all four sides (ceiling gap cols 14-17, floor gap cols 14-17, west and east gaps at row 14). Two tall solid pillars frame the interior — col 7 spanning rows 8-16 and col 24 spanning rows 5-14 — leaving a wide vertical gallery between them. Inside that gallery a loose zigzag of one-way platforms (row 13 cols 10-14, row 10 cols 17-21, row 7 cols 10-14, row 4 cols 18-24) forms an alternating left-right ascent from floor to ceiling; the middle of the room is otherwise empty air. A short stub platform at row 15 cols 4-8 bridges the west door past the left pillar.
hazards: None. Zero spike tiles of any kind; no shutters, no timed elements. The only failure state is a missed jump, and a missed jump just drops you to the flat floor to retry.
distinctive: It is the dungeon's crossing point — four doors, each leading somewhere different, with the ceiling route to Needle Room, a dash-gated east exit to Dash Chasm, and a coin-gated floor exit down to Underpass — so the room's real identity is navigational rather than mechanical. Coin 10 hangs at (188, 80), just above the mid-height right-hand platform, tempting you off the direct line.
archetype_guess: open hub chamber with staggered-platform vertical ascent

one_line: You stroll in from the west, hit a floor-to-ceiling wall that blocks the whole room, and have to turn a 5-tile-wide slot into a ~130px wall-jump chimney, cresting the barrier and then stepping down a ladder of one-way platforms to the east door.
structure: West-to-east transit split by a full-height divider at column 16 (rows 4-17): flat west approach under a hanging pillar (col 10, rows 4-12), a narrow vertical chimney between pillar and divider, an open crossing corridor along the top three rows, then a staged descent on the east side via one-way shelves at rows 6, 10 and 15 to the east door.
hazards: None — no spikes anywhere. All difficulty is geometric/technical: the only failure is falling back down the chimney and re-climbing.
distinctive: It is an explicit ability gate rather than a hazard room: the east door is locked behind the climbing gloves and a 10-coin requirement, and the layout physically cannot be crossed without a sustained left-right wall-jump chain — the room is the proficiency exam for the glove.
archetype_guess: gated wall-jump chimney (ability-check barrier room)

one_line: A calm, hazard-free cul-de-sac where you hop up a wide zigzag ladder of one-way platforms to grab a single coin tucked under the top-right ledge, then drop straight back out the floor you came in by.
structure: Single-door dead-end chamber (32x18) entered and exited through a floor gap at bottom-centre; travel is up-and-back-down a staircase of one-way platforms that alternate centre / left / centre / right / centre / far-right, ending at the coin near the top-right.
hazards: None at all — no spikes of any kind, no timed elements, no pits. The only failure mode is a mistimed hop that costs you a few seconds.
distinctive: Every surface in the room is a one-way platform, so the ascent is completely reversible and the return trip is a single uninterrupted free-fall down the middle of the room — a deliberate "pause and breathe" beat before the Sluice.
archetype_guess: no-hazard one-way-platform zigzag coin cul-de-sac (side-room treasure alcove)

one_line: A wide-open airy room you can stroll straight through in three seconds, unless you take the optional zig-zag ladder of one-way platforms up to the coin tucked at the top right, which asks for a dash-plus-jump on nearly every rung.
structure: 32x18 open hall with door gaps in both side walls at floor level (west and east, rows 14-16); the interior is empty air furnished only with five staggered one-way platforms forming a left-right-left-right ascent toward the top-right corner. Travel is horizontal for the mandatory route, vertical for the optional one.
hazards: Almost none: a single 2-tile up-spike bed on the floor at columns 17-18, easy to walk around or hop. No spike walls, no timed elements. Falling off the climb costs nothing but time.
distinctive: The vertical gaps (~30px) are comfortably within jump height but the horizontal offsets between consecutive rungs (~60-70px) exceed a plain jump, so the whole climb is a rhythm of dash-extended jumps in alternating directions — a dash ladder rather than a wall-jump chimney.
archetype_guess: optional dash-ladder coin climb over a trivial floor corridor

one_line: A tall, tense two-stage climb: you wall-jump out of a narrow chimney on the left, mantle a roof, throw a single mid-air dash rightward onto a hanging shelf, then wall-jump a second, narrower chimney to the ceiling ledge before dropping down a spike-mouthed shaft to the east door.
structure: A 32x18 vertical shaft complex read left-to-right but travelled up-over-down: west door and east door sit at the same low height (rows 13-15) but the entire floor between them is a spike bed, and a full-height pillar at column 24 walls the ground route off, so the only connection is over the top. Two stacked chimneys offset from each other — a wide one at cols 5-8 (between the col-4 wall and the col-9 pillar) on the left, a narrow 3-wide one at cols 21-23 (between the hanging col-20 pillar and the col-24 pillar) on the right — joined by a horizontal dash transfer at mid-height, and terminated by a 5-wide drop shaft (cols 25-29) down to the exit.
hazards: One continuous spike bed forms almost the whole floor: 14 tiles of upward spikes at cols 10-23 and another 3 at cols 25-27, split by the col-24 pillar. There are no timed or directional hazards — the spikes are pure consequence, punishing any missed wall-kick, short mantle, or an exit drop that isn't steered right onto the cols 28-30 landing strip. Nothing else in the room can kill you.
distinctive: The two climbing chimneys are deliberately offset rather than stacked, so a single dash is the only thing that connects them — the room can't be beaten with wall-jump alone or dash alone (the content tests assert both incomplete loadouts fail), and the dash lands mid-sequence between the fourth and fifth wall-kick, which makes it feel like a rung in the climb rather than a separate move.
archetype_guess: offset twin-chimney wall-jump ascent with a mandatory dash transfer, over a spike-floor void
